openDecisions: RESOLVED (2026-08-24, user-confirmed): Mark Bad -> impute. The row survives, so other tags and the label at that timestamp are preserved. Original text: CUTOFF SEMANTICS — mark Bad (hole for imputation), drop row, or winsorize/clamp. The three produce different row counts and different downstream imputation behaviour, and only the third is expressible with today's server operation set (see findings). Do not default to `clip` merely because it is the one that already exists.

RESOLVED (2026-08-24, user-confirmed): OFF, proposed per tag. Every toggle starts disabled; the engineer opts each tag in. Matches DS-LAKE-019's advisory precedent and the operating-window finding. Original text: DEFAULT STATE PER TAG — range cutoff ON by default (trusting the Excel range as authoritative) or OFF-and-proposed (engineer opts each tag in). Bound to the operating-window-vs-validity-range finding. DS-LAKE-019's blocking/advisory precedent argues for proposed-not-applied, but that is a recommendation, not a decision.

RESOLVED (2026-08-24, user-confirmed): Engineer picks; nothing applied until they do. Implemented structurally, not via a separate picker: a preset-range ConditionalRule's id is keyed by TAG ONLY (outlier-removal-panel.tsx's presetRangeRuleId), so enabling one duplicate-row candidate for a tag replaces any other candidate's rule for the same tag -- mutual exclusion for free, no extra state. Original text: MULTI-CONFIG CONFLICT — when one tag carries a range in more than one config_no: intersect (most conservative), union, last-applied-wins, or refuse and make the user pick. SD&TA's existing OR/AND combine mode is the nearest precedent.

ACCEPTED AS ASSUMPTION (2026-08-24, not reopened as a fork): out of scope at Step 3.2 -- the derived column does not exist until Step 4. The parsed struct is still emitted for equation features (range_parsed on every PresetFeature) so nothing vanishes; no Step 4 gate is built this session. Original text: EQUATION-FEATURE RANGES — deferred to a Step 4 gate on the derived column, or dropped from scope entirely with the reason recorded in the UI so `0.85-1.2` does not silently vanish.

RESOLVED (2026-08-24, user-confirmed): Import time, in Python. Implemented in apps/python/services/range_parser.py, wired into preset_parser.py's PresetFeature/preset_document; SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 1->2 (additive, nothing branches on it -- see T01). Original text: PARSE POINT — parse the range string at IMPORT time (Excel to preset JSON; warnings surface once, near the source; requires `schema_version` 1 to 2 and a decision on whether the raw string is retained alongside the parsed struct) or at APPLY time in the client (no schema change; every consumer re-parses and can drift). tasks.title: RangeBound parser written against the observed grammar, with failures into `parse_warnings[]`
tasks.scope_note: One pure function, unit-tested standalone BEFORE any UI or endpoint exists to call it — the discipline DS-LAKE-005B-A-T06 established for LTTB. tasks.result: apps/python/services/range_parser.py: parse_range(text) -> ParsedRange{kind, min, max, unit, raw}, plus range_parse_warning(parsed). tasks.title: Unit reconciliation gate against the tag catalog's own engineering unit
tasks.scope_note: The preset's range unit is compared against the unit the tag actually reports (TagItem already carries `unit` — apps/python/services/tag_service.py, per DS-LAKE-005B-A-T03's own grep note). Three outcomes, all explicit: units match (apply), units differ by a known scale factor (kg/hr vs tph, t vs kg) so offer the converted bound and show both numbers, units differ with no known conversion (refuse to apply and say why). A range with `unit: null` (`"0.85-1.2"`) is dimensionless and applies as-is. NEVER auto-convert without showing the engineer both the quoted and applied numbers — the 1000x error in this finding produces plausible values, so a silent conversion is as dangerous as a silent non-conversion.
tasks.result: apps/client/lib/range-cutoff.ts: reconcileRangeUnit(parsed, tagUnit) -> {verdict, applied, factor, quotedUnit, tagUnit}. Five verdicts: dimensionless (no quoted unit, applies as-is), match (normalized units equal, applies as-is), converted (known kg/h<->t/h or kg<->t factor, applied is BOTH shown alongside quoted), unknown-unit (no known conversion, applied:null, refuses), tag-unit-unknown (tag has no PI-resolved unit -- CSV-uploaded/manually-inserted tags -- applied:null unless dimensionless). Unit normalization collapses the observed synonyms (kg/hr|kg/h|kgph, tph|t/h, c|C|degC) before comparing. The engineering unit itself was found to die at Step 1: metaByTag is hook-local in use-dataset-tag-metadata.ts and Step 3 today fabricates units from a hardcoded 4-entry mock (lib/mock-readings.ts). DS-LAKE-005B-A-V01 closed by structural proof that AppZodValidationPipe runs before any controller body, so no artifact lookup has happened when validation fails. Raising it for export would remove that proof for every other caller of /rows. Export needs its own path, not a widened limit.

DROPPING THE __status SIBLING COLUMNS SILENTLY TURNS HOLES INTO ZEROS. frame_service.MISSING_VALUE is 0.0 and a Bad cell is stored as 0.0 with its status in the sibling column. A CSV carrying values without status is not a lossy export, it is a WRONG one -- a Bad cell reads as a real measurement of zero, and the reader has no way to tell. Every downstream consumer of that CSV inherits the error. This is the single most important decision in this feature and it is not a formatting preference.

KEEPING THE SIBLING COLUMNS DOUBLES THE WIDTH TO 2N+1. An 8,000-tag artifact exports 16,001 columns. Excel's hard ceiling is 16,384 columns, so it fits by 383 columns and nothing else will. pandas.read_csv handles it; most desktop tools do not.

FINAL AND ITS PARENT SHARE ONE OBJECT. promoteDraftArtifactToFinalService copies objectKey and checksum verbatim (DS-LAKE-012-V03 proved GOLD and FINAL share a checksum live), so 'export the FINAL' and 'export the GOLD' read the same bytes. Stating which stage the user is exporting is a UI honesty requirement, not a lookup detail.

THE HOLDOUT IS A SIBLING OBJECT, NOT PART OF data.parquet. validate_data.parquet sits beside BRONZE and its rows were CUT from the training path (DS-LAKE-018-T03). An export of the FINAL therefore silently omits the holdout rows -- correct for 'export what the model trained on', wrong for 'export my data'. Whichever is meant must be stated in the UI, because the row count will not match what the engineer fetched at Step 2.

A 2M-ROW EXPORT IS NOT AN INLINE CALL. validation on a 2M x 20 artifact took 4.25s (DS-LAKE-007-V03); a CSV serialise plus upload of the same frame is materially larger. materialize is already the inline-blocking 'can take minutes' call this slice records as a UX problem -- do not add a second one.
openDecisions: STATUS COLUMNS -- include (correct, 2N+1 wide, breaks most tools), drop (narrow, and silently reports Bad cells as 0.0), or drop-with-a-blank-cell substitution (narrow and honest, but changes the dtype of every column with any Bad cell). The third option is the recommendation on record, NOT adopted: an empty CSV field is the conventional NULL and every reader already handles it, whereas 0.0 is indistinguishable from data.

WHICH STAGE IS EXPORTABLE -- FINAL only, or any stage in the lineage. Exporting BRONZE is genuinely useful (raw as-fetched) and costs nothing extra since the object is pinned; exporting SILVER/GOLD is only meaningful while the objects survive retention. Offering a stage whose bytes were reclaimed produces a 404 at click time.

HOLDOUT ROWS -- omit (matches the FINAL artifact exactly), include as a second file, or include with a split marker column. A marker column re-introduces the leakage-by-convention shape userDecisions rejected for the sidecar itself, so it is the weakest of the three.

DELIVERY -- presigned MinIO URL (reuses presign_artifact/presignArtifact, already live on the model-run claim path, and keeps the bytes off both NestJS and the browser) vs. a streamed response through NestJS. Presign is the smaller change and the only one that does not put a multi-GB body through the Node process.

features.title: Reorder the wizard: EDA at Step 3, Feature Engineering at Step 4, Data Cleaning at Step 5 — and remap SILVER to features
features.description: Six steps: Verified Tags -> Fetch Data -> EDA -> Feature Engineering -> Data Cleaning -> Review & Save. Cleaning moves BEHIND feature engineering so a derived column's own range can be cut (DS-LAKE-020's own openDecisions[3], unresolvable while cleaning ran first), and SILVER becomes the feature stage while GOLD becomes the cleaned+scaled stage. Every existing panel keeps its layout; what changes is which step mounts it and what order the server stages run in.
features.audit_note: SCOPED AFTER READING feature_service.py DIRECTLY (2026-08-25), not from the ledger. Two premises this feature was drafted on were wrong and are corrected in the findings, one in each direction: derived-column status is BETTER than assumed (a real gate, not a silent Good), and to_model_ready is WORSE (it launders every Bad to Good, which makes the naive version of this reorder a complete no-op). One request in the original ask — putting the holdout SPLIT at Step 4 — is refused on leakage grounds and re-scoped to the picker only; see decisions.holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not.
findings: CORRECTED, AND IN THE PROJECT'S FAVOUR — DERIVED-COLUMN STATUS IS A REAL GATE, NOT A SILENT GOOD. An earlier framing of this reorder worried that apply_features might stamp every derived column Good, which would make cleaning-after-features pointless. Read directly: _compute_feature_column (feature_service.py) reads sources through _good_value, which returns None for a non-Good cell, and writes (0.0, STATUS_BAD) whenever any required source value is None. rolling additionally requires a COMPLETE window of Good values — its own `complete` flag plus a len(collected) < window check — so there is no partial average wearing a Good status. formula, ratio, arith, log, lag and delta all gate the same way. A derived column's Bad cells are therefore honest, and cleaning placed after feature engineering has something real to act on.

NEW AND LOAD-BEARING — to_model_ready LAUNDERS EVERY BAD CELL TO GOOD, SO THE NAIVE REORDER IS A NO-OP. The module's own docstring states it: 'toModelReady scales every FINITE value regardless of its ORIGINAL status and always emits Good afterward — a Bad cell holding a real (non-hole) number is silently laundered to Good by scaling.' Combined with the finding above, the consequence is exact: apply_features writes 0.0 for a Bad derived cell, 0.0 is finite, so to_model_ready scales it and forces STATUS_GOOD. Today's GOLD frame contains no Bad cells at all. Cleaning inserted AFTER features() as it currently stands would therefore see a frame that is uniformly Good and every drop_missing / mark rule would be a no-op. This is why DS-LAKE-022-T02 (split to_model_ready out to the end) is not an optimisation — it is the precondition for the whole feature.

NEW — A BAD CELL'S 0.0 IS FINITE, SO IT ENTERS EVERY SCALER'S OWN STATISTICS. _scale_column gates on np.isfinite alone; a Bad derived cell stored as 0.0 passes that gate. So minmax's min, standard's mean/std (via _welford_population_std's finite_in_order list) and robust's median/IQR are all computed INCLUDING the holes. A long Bad stretch under rolling(60) contributes a run of 0.0 values that drags min down and skews the mean. This is a pre-existing defect, not one this feature introduces — but the reorder FIXES it for free, because cleaning removes or fills those holes before any scaler sees them. Worth stating so the improvement is attributed correctly rather than discovered later as a mystery.

NEW — DROP-ROW IS SAFE ON A DERIVED COLUMN; VALUE-MODIFYING OPS ARE NOT. Dropping a row removes the derived value and its own sources together, so lag_5(TI202) still equals TI202 shifted by five across the surviving rows. Filling, clipping, winsorising or mark-then-impute does not: writing a mean into lag_5(TI202) makes that column no longer the thing its name claims, and every resulting number looks entirely plausible. Same silent-wrongness class as DS-LAKE-018's unpersisted scaler params and DS-LAKE-021's 0.0-reads-as-a-measurement. Resolved in decisions.value_ops_refused_on_derived_columns.

NEW — apply_features' NAME-COLLISION SKIP BECOMES USER-VISIBLE ONCE COLUMNS ARE SELECTABLE AT STEP 4. apply_features skips a config whose column name already exists (`if col in out.columns: continue`), appending it to `skipped` so artifact_service.features can keep feature_spec.json from claiming it (DS-LAKE-006-T06's own fix). A preset equation can legitimately mint a name that collides with a real tag. Once Step 4 offers explicit column selection, a user will see that feature absent from the list and have no way to distinguish 'I deselected it' from 'it collided and was never computed'. The skipped list already carries the answer; the Step 4 UI must surface it.

THE HOLDOUT'S SPLIT POINT AND THE HOLDOUT'S PICKER ARE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS, AND ONLY ONE CAN MOVE. Splitting after apply_features lets a rolling(60) window straddle the boundary — the holdout's own first rows would be computed partly from training rows, which is the exact window-straddling leakage MODEL-FLOW-009-T02 describes, and it destroys DS-LAKE-018's own stated purpose ('does this model work on data as it actually arrives'). The picker's POSITION carries no such constraint. DS-LAKE-018-T06 already built resplit_holdout precisely to let the picker live away from materialize time, walking up to the pristine BRONZE root and re-splitting from it — so moving the picker to Step 4 needs no new server capability at all.

DS-LAKE-016's STAGE-SUFFIXED FILENAMES BECOME ACTIVELY MISLEADING, WHICH IS WORSE THAN ABSENT. data_silver.parquet means 'cleaned' for every object written before this feature and 'feature-engineered' for every object after, and committed objects can never be renamed (immutable, checksum-bound — DS-LAKE-016's own second finding). DS-LAKE-016 exists to make a stage identifiable from a MinIO console without a Postgres round trip; after the reorder that same filename answers the question wrongly. Resolved in decisions.pipeline_version_makes_the_shift_readable.

THE STEP RENUMBERING TRAP IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED, FROM THE MODEL SIDE. MODEL-FLOW-010-T02 found that the wizard shell was not the only place holding step numbers: 'use-model-pipeline-nav.ts was the real trap' — nine separate setHighestUnlocked(prev => Math.min(prev, 2)) relock calls, plus an edit-mode hydration landing on a numeric step. The dataset wizard has the same shape (DW_TOTAL_STEPS, wizard-shell.tsx's labels, use-dataset-pipeline-nav's canAdvance chain, use-dataset-edit-hydration's landing step). Grep for every numeric step reference; do not assume the shell is the only one.

STEP 3 SPLITS IN TWO, AND THAT SPLIT — NOT THE RENUMBERING — IS THE REAL WORK. step-3-eda.tsx today mounts BOTH Step31EDA and Step32Imputation. The reorder sends their contents to opposite ends of the wizard: DataAnalysisCard and the readiness caption (DS-LAKE-015) stay at the new Step 3; the crop / conditional / statistical rule editors and the whole imputation scrubber move to the new Step 5 alongside OutlierRemovalPanel and DS-LAKE-020's preset range cutoff.

A READ-ONLY STEP 3 RESOLVES DS-LAKE-005B-D-V02 BY REMOVING ITS SUBJECT, NOT BY PASSING IT. V02 asks to 'change one crop or statistical rule and confirm the returned histogram bins and boxplot quartiles CHANGE' — still pending because every chart endpoint is called with operations: [] (recorded on DS-LAKE-005B-D-T01/T03 as gated on the separately-scoped precleanse port). Once the rule editors leave Step 3, operations: [] is CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION rather than a shortfall, and V02 no longer describes a state the product can be in. That is a re-scope, not a pass — record it as one.

DS-LAKE-005B-D-T08a's BLOCKER MAY DISSOLVE, BUT CHECK RATHER THAN ASSUME. It is blocked because clipBasis needs percentiles from 'the result of precleanse OMITTING valueClip' and the only server surface offering them is scrubber-gated. With crop and the scrubber both living at Step 5, that pre-clip position is likely addressable on demand. Likely is not verified — its own blockedReason asks for a full read of use-dataset-draft-pipeline's state machine, and that read is still owed.

CORRECTED IN THIS FEATURE'S OWN EXECUTION -- pipelineVersion's first shipped form was a lie waiting to happen. It went in as `Int? @default(2)` on the reasoning that a column default cannot be forgotten by a create site, which is true and was the wrong trade: a default encodes 'when the row was created', and this column means 'which code path produced it'. Those coincide only under a clean cutover, and this reorder is explicitly not one (decisions.both_orders_coexist_server_side). The next old-order artifact would have been stamped post-reorder. Fixed by a second migration dropping the default, with the value written explicitly at the two sites that know the order. Worth recording because the failure mode is this ledger's recurring one: a field added to make something readable, which instead asserts something false with more confidence than the ambiguity it replaced.

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED -- there are exactly TWO stage-decision sites in the backend, which is what T03's own scope_note asked someone to confirm before trusting 'inverting that one ternary is the core of it'. Grepping every `type: 'GOLD'` and `artifactKey(...)` call: preprocessing-job.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts's inline /features route. The scope_note was half right -- DS-LAKE-016-T04 did collapse the RUNNER's decision to one variable, but the runner then re-derived the same choice a second time inline for the object key, and the inline /features route was a third place entirely. artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts treats BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD symmetrically so it needs no change, and artifact-keys.ts's type union is positional.

T04-T07 IMPLEMENTATION (2026-08-25). The wizard is now 6 steps: Verified Tags -> Fetch -> EDA -> Feature Engineering -> Data Cleaning -> Review & Save. Cleaning's local preview now runs on applyFeatures(raw, featureConfigs) first — unconditionally in both modes, not mode-branched, since edit mode's featureConfigs is the hydrated/locked recipe and re-applying it reproduces the identical featured frame step-6's own legacy path already computes. Two real server bugs found and fixed as prerequisites: neither startDraftCleanJobService nor startDraftFeaturesJobService forwarded scaleRecipe/scale onto the stored job payload, so T02/T03's reordered runner branch was correct but permanently unreachable from any client until this pass. A pipelineVersion guard (422) was added to startDraftCleanJobService so a scaleRecipe can only target a source actually produced by the reordered FEATURE stage.

GAPS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, NOT SILENTLY DROPPED: (1) skipped_features display surfacing (T05's own second half) — the data is already in artifact_service.features's response, only the Step 4 UI read of it is missing. (2) value-op-refused-on-derived-columns enforcement (T06's decisions.value_ops_refused_on_derived_columns, which V03 depends on) — ImputationDetailPanel today accepts any value-modifying step against any tag including derived ones; needs reading feature_spec.json's recorded feature names to distinguish derived from raw columns at the UI layer. (3) V06's full browser walkthrough. All three are why the feature stays in_progress, not completed.

holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not.chosen: The holdout PICKER moves to Step 4; the holdout SPLIT stays at BRONZE
holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not.rationale: The stated reason for moving it — being able to see and cut newly created and equation-derived columns — is a column-selection concern, and select_columns already operates on exactly those columns at Step 4. Moving the SPLIT itself would let a rolling window straddle the boundary (see findings), which is a different and much worse problem than the one being solved. Splitting at BRONZE also costs nothing to keep: DS-LAKE-018-T06 already built resplit_holdout for a picker that lives away from materialize time, and replay_holdout already replays the feature recipe onto raw holdout rows, so the reorder needs no replay change whatsoever.
holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not.consequence: The Step 4 picker renders the SAME ValidationHoldoutSection component, moved, and calls the SAME resplit endpoint. value_ops_refused_on_derived_columns.chosen: Drop-row operations apply to any column; value-modifying operations are refused on derived columns
value_ops_refused_on_derived_columns.rationale: Per the findings: dropping a row keeps a derived column consistent with its sources, filling or clipping breaks the relationship its own name asserts, and does so invisibly. Refusing is the smaller and more honest option, and matches this codebase's established discipline of refusing with a stated reason rather than warning (assert_target_is_unscaled, replay_holdout's lead-in check, DS-LAKE-020's unit-reconciliation gate).

rejected.Allow everything with a warning: A warning on a screen where the number still looks right is the failure mode this project has now recorded three times (unpersisted scaler params, 0.0-as-measurement, mark-Bad on an operating window).
rejected.Recompute dependent derived columns afte: Correct in principle and needs a dependency graph over feature configs. Genuinely larger than this feature; recorded as future work, not attempted.

value_ops_refused_on_derived_columns.note: A derived column is identifiable without new bookkeeping: feature_column_name's output is exactly the set of columns apply_features minted, and feature_spec.json already records every computed feature by name.

pipeline_version_makes_the_shift_readabl.chosen: Additive DatasetArtifact.pipelineVersion Int?, null meaning pre-reorder
pipeline_version_makes_the_shift_readabl.rationale: The DatasetArtifactType enum needs no migration — it is positional, and SILVER simply means 'stage 2', which is now features. What DOES break is DS-LAKE-016's filename diagnosability: the same data_silver.parquet means two different things either side of this feature, and existing objects cannot be renamed. A version column makes that shift READABLE rather than invisible, which is the same reason SCHEMA_VERSION and FEATURE_SPEC_VERSION exist in this codebase already.

rejected.Rename the stage filenames: Forbidden — committed objects are immutable and checksum-bound (DS-LAKE-016's own finding), and renaming would mean copying bytes, which global_definition_of_done rules out.
rejected.Add new enum members: A second axis of meaning for the same four positions, and every existing consumer's switch would need widening for no gain.

layout_is_preserved_placement_is_not.note: Explicit user instruction: keep every panel's existing layout. So this feature moves components between steps and does not redesign any of them. The two places where that is not literally achievable are stated rather than glossed: Step 3 loses its rule editors (they move to Step 5 — that IS the reorder, not a layout change), and Step 4 gains the holdout section plus a column-selection surface it did not have.

scale_split_lands_additively_first.chosen: DS-LAKE-022-T02 ships FeaturesRequest.scale (default True) plus a separate ScaleRequest/scale()/POST /v1/preprocess/scale, and changes NO existing caller. The artifactType stage inversion in preprocessing-job.service.ts is deferred to land together with the Step 3/4 wizard reorder (T04-T07), not with T02/T03.
scale_split_lands_additively_first.rationale: feature_service.DEFAULT_SCALER is 'minmax', and to_model_ready() scales every column even when scalers={} is passed -- there is no 'pass nothing, scale nothing' shortcut. With the wizard still at 5 steps, an unconditional stage inversion would route the CLEAN job's output through the new scale endpoint at Step 3.2 time, BEFORE Step 4 has authored any feature config or scaler choice -- silently min-max scaling the frame on an empty recipe, then computing lag/rolling/ratio features on already-scaled values at Step 4. This is worse than doing nothing: it corrupts data on the branch before any UI change ships to prove it wrong. The repo already has precedent for landing a capability additively and cutting over later -- PreprocessingJob's legacy sourceVersion pointer ('kept until DS-LAKE-009 reshapes DatasetVersion, so existing job rows stay readable and the build stays green') is the same shape.
scale_split_lands_additively_first.consequence: V01 and V04 are provable THIS session because the new Python tests call features(scale=False) -> clean() -> scale() directly, bypassing the TS job runner entirely. The wizard's actual UI-driven flow is unaffected until T04-T07 lands the inversion in the same deploy as the Step 3/4 UI that makes it correct -- do not merge the stage inversion to main without that UI change alongside it.

feature_spec_ownership_moves_to_scale_st.chosen: feature_spec.json is written ONLY by scale() (or by features(scale=True), which still owns it in the pre-cutover combined path). features(scale=False) writes no sidecar at all.
feature_spec_ownership_moves_to_scale_st.rationale: Resolves openDecisions[1] ('feature_spec.json ownership once to_model_ready moves'). build_feature_spec (feature_spec_service.py:197) is pure -- features, selected_columns, scalers, target_y, scaling_params, no frame -- so it can be built entirely at whichever stage actually runs to_model_ready, with no risk of two stages racing to write it or one stage writing a partial spec.
feature_spec_ownership_moves_to_scale_st.consequence: Resolves openDecisions[2] as a side effect, not a separate change: featureSpecKey still lands on the GOLD row exactly as before, model-run.authorized.service.ts's non-GOLD refusal is untouched, and replay_holdout_for_run needs no key forwarding or parent walk.

both_orders_coexist_server_side.chosen: Both pipeline orders run simultaneously, selected PER JOB by the stored recipe -- a FEATURE job with `scale: false` or a CLEAN job with a `scaleRecipe` takes the reordered path; everything else takes the legacy one. No global flip, no server flag, no deploy ordering.
both_orders_coexist_server_side.rationale: The reorder cannot be a single atomic flip, because the thing that decides the order is the CLIENT's step sequence and the server cannot see which wizard version is talking to it. Flipping the stage ternary alone would have been actively destructive while the 5-step wizard is live: Step 3.2's clean job would run the new scaling tail with `scalers={}`, and DEFAULT_SCALER is 'minmax', so an empty dict scales every column rather than skipping -- then Step 4 computes lag/rolling/ratio on already-scaled values. Making the order a property of the request removes the coupling entirely: the server supports both, and T04-T07 becomes a pure client change.
both_orders_coexist_server_side.consequence: pipelineVersion CANNOT have a column default under this decision -- see the T03 result for the defect that caused and its correcting migration. Every test in this area comes in pairs (legacy shape untouched, reordered shape takes the new path), because a suite that only exercised the new path would not notice the old one breaking. The legacy path is dead weight the moment T04-T07 ships, and should be REMOVED then rather than left as a permanent second code path.

decisions.edit_mode_stays_legacy_order: Edit mode's only editable surface is the preprocessing pipeline (features/tags/time-range are locked, hydrated for display only per wizard-shell.tsx's own isEditLocked gate) — so it never opts into the reorder. useDatasetGoldWarm sends no `scale` field in edit mode (legacy combined write, writes dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom directly) and step-5-data-cleaning.tsx's Save button still calls useDatasetDraftPipeline.applyClean (chains onto BRONZE per batch), exactly as before this feature existed. Only CREATE mode takes T02/T03's reordered server path. This was a design call made explicitly this session (not in the original ask), reasoned from: forcing a locked surface through a re-derivation server round-trip on every edit-mode session would add real latency and risk for zero product benefit — nothing about editing a saved dataset's cleaning pipeline requires the reorder's benefit (letting a NEW recipe's cleaning target a NEW derived column), since edit mode cannot add new features at all.
decisions.three_pointer_artifact_chain: New atom dwDraftFeatureArtifactIdAtom holds create-mode's reordered-order features-only SILVER, kept SEPARATE from both dwDraftArtifactIdAtom (stays the fixed BRONZE every Step-5 clean batch replays against, per D4) and dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom (the real, final GOLD Step 5's clean+scale job produces). Stays null in edit mode by construction (edit_mode_stays_legacy_order above) — every existing reader (useDatasetValidation's gateArtifactId = gold ?? silver, DataAnalysisCard's analysisArtifactId, step-6's metadataArtifactId/goldNotReady) needed ZERO changes, because 'GOLD-if-present-else-draft' was already the correct fallback shape — only WHICH stage writes to WHICH atom changed, not the fallback logic itself.
decisions.step5_commit_is_explicit_not_debounced: useDatasetCleaningScaleCommit fires ONCE on advancing past Step 5 (create mode only), not on a debounced timer like useDatasetGoldWarm — preserves the wizard's existing 'local preview, server on Apply' UX contract rather than reversing it into a background auto-save. Also covers the zero-cleaning-rules case for free: an empty cleaningPipelines still sends scaleRecipe with no operations, which StartCleanJobSchema's own doc comment already declares legal (a draft with features but no cleaning rules still needs its GOLD written).

openDecisions: RESOLVED (user-confirmed, 2026-08-25): the original ask behind 'put the holdout at Feature Engineering' is the picker move ALONE -- Step 4 renders the same ValidationHoldoutSection, same resplit endpoint, split still cut at BRONZE (decisions.holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not, unchanged). The derived-column-coverage read (how much of a candidate holdout window a lag(5)/rolling(60) column is Bad for) is explicitly NOT part of this feature and is not built -- record as its own future ledger entry if the coverage-at-pick-time need resurfaces, rather than silently building or silently dropping it.
feature_spec.json OWNERSHIP -- RESOLVED, see decisions.feature_spec_ownership_moves_to_scale_stage.

WHICH ARTIFACT model-run READS -- RESOLVED, and the original premise was FACTUALLY WRONG. This entry claimed 'model-run.service.ts refuses any non-GOLD artifact'. It does not: model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts's buildRunData refuses any artifact whose type is not FINAL ('Training reads the dataset's committed FINAL artifact -- save the dataset first'). Training never reads GOLD directly, so the stage swap cannot affect it. The finalize path is stage-agnostic too -- it promotes whatever artifact id it is handed, copying objectKey, checksum, columnStatsKey and featureSpecKey onto the FINAL without inspecting the source's type -- so both orders produce an identical FINAL as long as the last stage before it carries featureSpecKey, which under the reorder the trailing scale call now does. No resolver change, no key forwarding, no parent walk. pipelineVersion is now copied onto FINAL as well, which is what T08 will read.

tasks.title: Remap the artifact stages and make the shift readable
tasks.scope_note:
BRONZE unchanged (raw). SILVER becomes features. GOLD becomes cleaned + scaled. FINAL unchanged (a pointer promotion of GOLD, no bytes — DS-LAKE-012-V03 proved they share a checksum).

The code change is smaller than it sounds: DS-LAKE-016-T04 already collapsed the stage decision into ONE variable (`artifactType = isFeatureJob ? 'GOLD' : 'SILVER'` in preprocessing-job.service.ts), reused for both the object key and the row's own type. Inverting that one ternary is the core of it. Verify there is no second, independent stage decision elsewhere before assuming that.

Add DatasetArtifact.pipelineVersion Int? per decisions.pipeline_version_makes_the_shift_readable — additive, nullable, null meaning pre-reorder. It is what stops data_silver.parquet from being an unmarked lie for the rest of this system's life.
tasks.result:
COMPLETED 2026-08-25. The stage remap is implemented, reachable and tested; the earlier deferral is lifted. What changed since that deferral is the mechanism, not the caution behind it: instead of FLIPPING the pipeline order globally (which, with the 5-step wizard still live, would have min-max scaled a frame at Step 3.2 on an empty scalers dict and then computed lag/rolling/ratio on scaled values), both orders now run SIDE BY SIDE and each job picks one from the recipe it was given.

THE STAGE DECISION IS NOW DATA-DRIVEN AND SINGULAR. preprocessing-job.service.ts computes `artifactType` exactly once, AFTER reading the stored payload, and derives `committedKey` from that same value -- the old code had two independent ternaries (one for the row's type at :214, a second inline for the object key at :228) which could drift into a row typed GOLD whose key said silver. A job is REORDERED iff its own payload says so: a FEATURE job carrying `scale: false`, or a CLEAN job carrying a `scaleRecipe`. Every client that exists today sends neither and gets the legacy order byte for byte, proven by paired tests (RMP-01/02, RMP-07/08).

  legacy   BRONZE -> clean(SILVER) -> features+scale(GOLD) -> FINAL
  reorder  BRONZE -> features(SILVER) -> clean+scale(GOLD) -> FINAL

CLEAN JOB GAINED THE SCALING TAIL. Under the reorder every cleaning operation writes to tmp/ (including the last one -- the `isLast` special case is suppressed) and a trailing /v1/preprocess/scale call writes the committed GOLD key. Getting that wrong would have written the committed key twice, and put_frame refuses to overwrite a committed key, so the job would fail AFTER paying for all the work; RMP-03 pins it. Zero-operation clean jobs are now legal when a scaleRecipe is present (a draft with features but no cleaning rules still needs its GOLD) -- `StartCleanJobSchema.operations` lost its `.min(1)`, with the refusal preserved one layer later at the runner's existing `if (!stats)` guard so an empty job with no scaleRecipe still FAILS rather than committing an artifact nothing was applied to (RMP-06).

PAYLOAD KEY IS `scaleRecipe`, NOT `features`, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. readOperations refuses any payload with a top-level `features` key and no `operations` ('this is a feature recipe, refusing to run as CLEAN'), and readFeatureRecipe refuses the mirror image. Those guards are what make `features` mean 'this row is a FEATURE job'. Reusing that key for the scaling tail would have tripped them on every reordered clean job, and the alternative -- loosening a guard whose stated purpose is catching a mis-routed payload -- is the trade this ledger keeps refusing. A malformed scaleRecipe throws rather than degrading to the legacy order (RMP-09): degrading silently would commit SILVER bytes under a pipelineVersion the row does not carry.

featureSpecKey NOW READ FROM WHICHEVER CALL WROTE THE ARTIFACT. The old `isFeatureJob ? stats.feature_spec_key : null` would have discarded the sidecar key under the reorder, because there the sidecar is written by the trailing SCALE call on a CLEAN job -- leaving the GOLD row with featureSpecKey null, which /finalize then copies onto FINAL, which replay_holdout_for_run needs to score a holdout at all. RMP-04 pins it.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS TASK'S OWN EARLIER OUTPUT: pipelineVersion shipped as `Int? @default(2)`, on the reasoning that a column default cannot be forgotten by a create site. That reasoning assumed a clean cutover. Under coexistence it is actively wrong -- the very next OLD-order artifact would have been stamped 'post-reorder', turning the one column meant to make the stage shift readable into a more confident lie than the filename it exists to explain. Corrected by migration 20260825101500_ds_lake_022_t03_pipeline_version_no_default (DROP DEFAULT); the value is now written explicitly by the two sites that know which order ran, and NULL keeps its documented meaning. Caught before any row was written: verified 96 rows, 96 NULL, zero stamped 2 at the moment of the fix.

ONLY TWO STAGE-DECISION SITES EXIST -- the ledger's own 'verify there is no second, independent stage decision' check, now actually performed rather than assumed. Grepped every `type: 'GOLD'` and `artifactKey(...)` call in the backend: preprocessing-job.service.ts (the job runner) and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts:571 (the inline /features route). Both updated. artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts treats BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD symmetrically as draft-owned intermediates, so the swap needs no change there; artifact-keys.ts's type union is positional and needs none either.

FINAL NOW CARRIES pipelineVersion, copied from the artifact it promotes. A FINAL is a pointer promotion (same objectKey, same checksum -- DS-LAKE-012-V03), so it was produced by whichever order produced its source. This is the field T08 reads to choose a replay order, and a FINAL that dropped it would send a pre-reorder dataset down the post-reorder replay path and break the byte-identical checksum reproducibility DS-LAKE-012-T10 proved.

VERIFIED: 9 new backend tests (RMP-01..09) all green; preprocessing-job.service.spec.ts 40/40; all 5 dataset-related backend suites 147/147; python suite 745 passed / 74 skipped with the one pre-existing unrelated failure unchanged; backend+client tsc clean apart from 4 pre-existing auth spec errors in files this work never touched. Backend->Python payload contract checked against the REAL Python schema (not a mock): ScaleRequest accepts the runner's exact body including the camelCase `selectedColumns` alias beside snake_case `source_key`/`target_y`, FeaturesRequest honours explicit `scale: false` and defaults to True when the key is absent, and /v1/preprocess/scale is registered on the app.

STILL DEFERRED TO T04-T07, DELIBERATELY: no client sends the new-order fields yet, so nothing in production takes the reordered path. That is the point -- the server half is complete and independently provable, and the wizard renumber becomes a pure client change (send `scale: false` at the feature step, send a `scaleRecipe` from the cleaning step, renumber the steps) with ZERO further backend work required.

tasks.title: Recipe persistence and legacy hydration
tasks.scope_note:
PipelineConfig's field set does not change — the same crop/exclusions/conditionalRules/scalers/featureConfigs are recorded, only the ORDER they are applied in differs. So the persisted recipe cannot distinguish a pre-reorder dataset from a post-reorder one, and replaying an old recipe under the new order produces a DIFFERENT artifact.

That matters concretely: DS-LAKE-012-T10 proved reproducibility by replaying a pinned BRONZE plus its recorded operations to a byte-identical FINAL checksum. After this feature, that replay reproduces the old checksum only if it replays in the OLD order. Carry T03's pipelineVersion into the recipe (or read it off the artifact) so a replay knows which order to use. An unversioned legacy recipe must replay in the legacy order — silently replaying it in the new one would break the single strongest reproducibility claim this ledger holds.

acceptance_criteria: The wizard has six steps in the stated order, and this file's own definition of done says six rather than five.
Step 3 mounts no control that mutates a recipe; its chart calls pass operations: [] and that is correct rather than a gap.
A derived column can be deselected at Step 4, and a feature absent because of a name collision is distinguishable from one the user deselected.
The holdout picker renders at Step 4 and the holdout rows are still cut at BRONZE — provable by the same by-timestamp assertion DS-LAKE-018-V01 uses.
A drop-row cleaning operation applies to a derived column; a value-modifying one is refused with a stated reason.
An equation feature's range is appliable at Step 5, and a derived column with no reconcilable unit is refused by the existing gate rather than applied.
GOLD is the cleaned-and-scaled stage and SILVER is the feature stage; no existing object is renamed or rewritten.
pipelineVersion distinguishes a pre-reorder artifact from a post-reorder one, and a legacy recipe replays in the legacy order.
A cleaned-then-scaled GOLD's scalingParams are fit on cleaned rows, and the holdout is replayed with those same params.
Every panel that moved kept its layout.

features.title: Split the validation holdout AFTER feature engineering — one feature-bearing validate_data.parquet, no replay
features.description: The holdout is picked and cut at the Feature Engineering step, after Apply Feature, so validate_data.parquet carries the derived columns and their computed values — not raw rows a replay has to reconstruct. One file, not two. Cleaning then runs at the next step on the train side only; the holdout is never cleaned.
features.why_not_reopening_ds_lake_018: DS-LAKE-018 is completed at 100% with five live-verified verification items, including two (V01, V05) proven against real Postgres/MinIO/FastAPI. Reopening it to change its own split point would make its own completion claim false and mix verified history with unstarted work — the same reasoning MODEL-FLOW-011's first finding gives for staying out of MODEL-FLOW-002, and the same reasoning DS-LAKE-014 gives for being a separate feature from DS-LAKE-009B's cleanup mechanism. This feature supersedes specific parts of DS-LAKE-018 and says which; DS-LAKE-018's own entry gains a superseded_by note and nothing else.
features.reversal_note: REVERSES DS-LAKE-022's decisions.holdout_ui_moves_split_does_not, with both versions kept visible per DS-LAKE-005B-D's own correction convention. That decision refused to move the split on leakage grounds ('a rolling(60) window would straddle the boundary'). It was WRONG, and the reason it was wrong is in the code, not in the ledger: every kind in _compute_feature_column reads its own row or earlier rows only — lag reads i-k, delta reads i-1, rolling reads max(0, i-window+1)..i, and ratio/arith/log/formula/datetime read row i alone. Nothing reads forward. So computing features on the continuous frame and splitting afterwards yields exactly the values production would produce, because production's own new rows also read backwards into training-era history. DS-LAKE-018's HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN already conceded this point structurally: it COPIES seven days of training rows into the holdout sidecar specifically so the holdout's features can be computed. If a holdout's features seeing training rows were leakage, lead-in was leakage from the start. It is not.
findings: THE REAL LEAKAGE BOUNDARY IS PER-ROW-CAUSAL VERSUS WHOLE-COLUMN-FIT, NOT FEATURES VERSUS CLEANING. Safe before a split: apply_features (every kind, verified causal above), select_columns, and any rule with a CONSTANT bound (crop, exclude, a conditional rule on a fixed number, DS-LAKE-020's preset ranges). Unsafe before a split, because they fit a statistic over the column: to_model_ready's four scalers (minmax's min/max, standard's Welford mean/std, robust's Tukey median/IQR), fill_mean, fill_median, remove_outlier (which replaces with mean/median), zscore, and any percentile-derived clip bound. DS-LAKE-018-T02 exists precisely because the second group fails silently — 'scaling the holdout against its OWN statistics is a DIFFERENT transform from the one the model learned'. This feature moves the split across the first group only.

NEW AND THE MOST DANGEROUS THING HERE — AN UNCLEANED HOLDOUT FEEDS SCALED ZEROS INTO predict(). _compute_feature_column writes (0.0, STATUS_BAD) for every derived cell whose sources are not all Good, and rolling additionally demands a COMPLETE window of Good values. A short sensor dropout therefore produces a run of Bad derived cells as long as the window. Under decision (a) the holdout is never cleaned, so those 0.0 holes survive; to_model_ready gates on np.isfinite alone, so it scales them and forces STATUS_GOOD (its own docstring: 'a Bad cell holding a real (non-hole) number is silently laundered to Good by scaling'). The model then predicts from a fabricated zero and the holdout score is depressed with no trace of why. This is pre-existing — the old replay path called to_model_ready too — but decision (a) makes it STRUCTURAL rather than incidental, so it must be handled here. See T05.

THE SEAM IN THE TRAIN FRAME IS FIXED FOR FREE, AND THAT IS A REAL IMPROVEMENT, NOT A SIDE NOTE. Today _split_holdout cuts the holdout out of data.parquet BEFORE features run, so a mid-window holdout leaves train in two pieces and lag/rolling computed across that gap silently read rows from the wrong side of it (DS-LAKE-018-T01's guard 4 warns about this and deliberately does not block, since holding out a specific upset period is legitimate). With features computed on the continuous frame first, no derived value ever spans the cut. The guard's warning becomes advisory about the TRAINING DISTRIBUTION rather than about wrong feature values.

LEAD-IN AND THE LOOKBACK REFUSAL BECOME LEGACY-ONLY, AND MUST NOT BE DELETED. HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN (7 days), max_replay_lookback's compound-lookback walk, and replay_holdout's hard refusal all exist to make a RAW holdout computable. A feature-bearing holdout needs none of them. But every validate_data.parquet written before this feature is raw and still needs all three to be scoreable, so they stay — as the legacy path, not as dead code. Deleting them would make every pre-existing saved dataset unscoreable.

ONE FILENAME, TWO MEANINGS — THE DS-LAKE-016 PROBLEM AGAIN, ONE LAYER UP. validate_data.parquet means 'raw holdout, replay required' for every object written before this feature and 'feature-bearing holdout, scale-and-score' after, and committed objects can never be renamed. DS-LAKE-022-T03's pipelineVersion was proposed for diagnosability; here it becomes load-bearing for CORRECTNESS, because claim() must choose between the replay path and the direct path and cannot infer which from the object. A second, weaker discriminator falls out of the key structure — sidecar_key places the file beside whichever artifact wrote it, so a legacy holdout sits beside a BRONZE data key and a new one beside a SILVER data key — but that is inference from a path, and the row-level version is the one to depend on. VERIFY the sidecar_key claim against the actual write site rather than trusting this finding.

PRISTINE SILVER MUST SURVIVE THE WIZARD SESSION, BUT NEEDS NO LINEAGE PIN. _split_holdout is lossy (DS-LAKE-018-T06's own reasoning: once a holdout is applied, data.parquet no longer contains those rows, and the previous boundary is not recoverable), so re-splitting must always start from a never-split source. That source is now the pre-split SILVER rather than the pristine BRONZE. Unlike BRONZE it does NOT need a retention pin: apply_features is deterministic, so pristine SILVER is exactly reproducible from the pinned BRONZE plus the recorded recipe. The ACTIVE-draft retention window already covers the only period resplit can happen in.

CHANGING THE FEATURE RECIPE AFTER PICKING A HOLDOUT INVALIDATES THE HOLDOUT, AND THE ORDERING IS NOW USER-VISIBLE. Under the old design the two were independent — the split was raw, the recipe was replayed later. Now the holdout's own bytes contain the derived columns, so editing a feature config after the split makes the sidecar describe a recipe that no longer exists. This is a new sequencing constraint inside one step, and the step's own UI is the only place it can be expressed.

THE HOLDOUT STOPS BEING AN END-TO-END PIPELINE TEST AND BECOMES A MODEL TEST — ACCEPTED, RECORDED, NOT DISCOVERED LATER. DS-LAKE-018's own first finding stated the trade in the opposite direction: 'the replay in T04 is deliberately the same work production must do on every incoming batch, which makes this an end-to-end pipeline validation rather than a model-only one. That is a feature of the choice, not a workaround for it.' With one feature-bearing file and no replay, nothing exercises the apply-recipe-to-a-new-batch path anymore. A production bug in that path — a missing tag, a changed interval, a frame-shape difference — will no longer be caught by the holdout. This is the cost of the decision, chosen knowingly.

IMPLEMENTATION (2026-08-25), T01-T04+T06. Found and fixed the same class of 'DTO field never forwarded onto the stored job payload' bug DS-LAKE-022 hit twice — this time on the NEW `holdout` field on `CreateFeaturesSchema`, at `startDraftFeaturesJobService`'s create site. Found (not previously known): `validationHoldoutFrom` was written by only 1 of 3 legacy holdout writers — both materialize paths set `validationRowCount`/`validationMissingPct` but omit `validationHoldoutFrom`, and both consumers (`tryReplayHoldout`, `getArtifactHoldoutService`) hard-bail on that null — meaning a holdout picked at fetch time was invisible to replay/the holdout panel even before this feature. Not fixed here (legacy writers untouched, out of this feature's scope) — noted so it is not mistaken for new breakage. Found and fixed: `tryReplayHoldout`'s BRONZE-sibling resolver used an unordered `findFirst` — a draft resplit more than once can leave two artifacts sharing one `runId`; the rewritten resolver orders by `createdAt: 'desc'`.

EDIT-MODE RE-SPLIT AUDIT (2026-08-26), SESSION FOLLOWING T06's OWN COMPLETION CLAIM. T06 marked the edit-mode holdout picker wired via the legacy BRONZE-resplit path (`useDatasetHoldoutResplit`). It was never actually reachable: the picker's own `disabled` gate (`previewFetchState !== 'ready'`) becomes true, in a fresh edit session, ONLY via `useDatasetFeaturePreviewSample`'s DATASET LEG (`adoptedBronzeArtifactId` present, `dwDraftArtifactIdAtom` NULL) — and `useDatasetHoldoutResplit`'s own guard (`if (!draftId) return`, before `setStatus('pending')`) requires `dwDraftIdAtom` NON-null. Enabled implies the resplit call returns before doing anything; the resplit call being real implies the section is still disabled. Apply wrote the atom, rendered no error, and contacted the server never. This was true in every edit session, unconditionally — not an edge case.

TWO ADDITIONAL BUGS FOUND ALONGSIDE THE DEAD RESPLIT, ALL FIXED THIS SESSION EXCEPT WHERE NOTED. (a) `useDatasetGoldWarm` returned `void` — no pending/settled signal existed for a consumer to render "Applying…", gate navigation, or gate what Step 5 commits. FIXED: now returns `{warm, status, error}`, publishing `dwFeatureWarmStateAtom`/`dwFeatureArtifactStampAtom`. (b) `goTo` (the step indicator) never called `canAdvance` — a holdout Applied on Step 4 then immediately followed by a step-indicator jump to Step 5 could let `useDatasetCleaningScaleCommit` clean+scale the STALE pre-holdout feature artifact (AC3 violation). FIXED: `commit()` itself now refuses unless `dwFeatureWarmStateAtom==='ready'` AND the current recipe's `featureRecipeStamp` matches what the committed artifact was actually built from — the load-bearing gate, since it survives every navigation path including the indicator; `canAdvance`'s own Next-button gate is secondary. (c) `dwHoldoutRangeAtom` still fed `materialize`'s own BRONZE-stage holdout in BOTH `useDatasetBronzeWarm` and `useDatasetDraftPipeline`'s `ensureBronze` — after any BRONZE re-materialize, the feature-stage split ran a SECOND time: same window raised a hard 0-row refusal from Python's `features()`, a changed window silently wrote two `validate_data.parquet` objects with two rows carrying `validationRowCount`. FIXED: both call sites now pass `holdoutRange: null` unconditionally; the holdout is cut at the features stage only, in both modes, so BRONZE stays pristine.

UNIFYING EDIT MODE ONTO THE FEATURE-BEARING SPLIT WAS ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED MID-SESSION — NOT SHIPPED. The natural-looking fix (seed `dwDraftArtifactIdAtom` with a fresh BRONZE via `ensureDraft`/`ensureBronze` at Step 4 mount, matching what Step 5's own edit-mode cleaning already does) is WRONG: in edit mode that atom is the pipeline's CHAINED source — `useDatasetDraftPipeline.applyClean` advances it to the CLEANED SILVER once Step 5 runs, not a pinned BRONZE the way create mode keeps it. Seeding it with raw BRONZE at Step 4 makes the features+scale warm run on UNCLEANED rows the instant it fires, silently skipping cleaning for any edit-mode holdout — a real regression, caught before shipping via a second-opinion review, not by a test. There is also no stored pointer to the pre-features CLEANED artifact of a dataset's original run to adopt instead: `adoptedBronzeArtifactId` (`dataset.authorized.service.ts`'s own `artifacts` select, `where: {type:'BRONZE', objectReclaimedAt:null}`) names only the RAW lineage root. See DS-LAKE-023-T08 for the two real remaining options, neither built this session. RESOLUTION (2026-08-26): the revert was correct and stays reverted — seeding dwDraftArtifactIdAtom with a fresh BRONZE at Step 4 mount is still wrong for the reason stated above. T08 is closed as superseded by DS-LAKE-024 instead: giving edit mode its OWN real draft (rooted at the adopted BRONZE, not a client-side atom seed) makes the chained-source behavior applyClean already relies on become correct by construction, because the draft then follows create mode's own step order rather than trying to retrofit one atom to mean two different things.

decisions.discriminator_is_row_type_not_pipeline_v: D1. See DS-LAKE-023-T04's own completion note above.
decisions.create_mode_only: D2. Mirrors DS-LAKE-022's own mode split exactly, for the same reason: edit mode's feature recipe is locked (features/tags/time-range hydrated for display only), so it can never benefit from a reorder that exists to let a NEW feature's range be applied to a NEW holdout. Edit mode's holdout stays on the legacy BRONZE-split path, unchanged, forever (until/unless a future feature unlocks edit-mode feature editing, at which point this decision should be revisited, not assumed to still hold).
decisions.auto_resplit_on_recipe_change: D3. Chosen over locking the feature editors once a holdout exists (the ledger's own 'more honest' alternative) and over a third, warn-plus-explicit-recut option this session introduced. Falls out nearly free per the T02 correction: the features job already re-derives fully from BRONZE on every recipe edit, so making `dwHoldoutRangeAtom` a dependency of that SAME debounced effect costs nothing new and makes a stale holdout structurally unreachable (see V07's own note) rather than something to detect.
decisions.target_row_exclusion_covers_both_sides: D4. `train.py`'s holdout scoring block excludes non-Good TARGET rows the same way the train/test split already does (extracted into a shared `labelled_mask` function), reporting `dropped_unlabelled` beside the holdout metrics. This is separate from, and does not resolve, T05's own non-Good FEATURE row question — see T05's own scope_note.
decisions.t05_deferred_but_its_first_open_decision: D5. When T05 is built, exclusion must cover BOTH the train/test side and the holdout side, with counts reported on both — chosen explicitly over holdout-only (which the ledger's own finding warned would make the two scores incomparable in a new way while looking like a fix) and over deferring entirely (rejected because decision (a), 'the holdout is never cleaned', makes the scaled-zero path STRUCTURAL, per the ledger's own pre-existing finding). The write-time-vs-score-time question stays genuinely undecided.
decisions.t05_write_time_not_score_time_resolved: D6. Answers T05's own second openDecision. `to_model_ready` (feature_service.py) scales every FINITE value regardless of its ORIGINAL status and always forces Good afterward — the Bad-cell evidence this exclusion depends on is destroyed the instant scaling runs. There is no score-time option: by the time any reader sees the frame again, the row already looks like a normal Good observation. `drop_bad_feature_rows` (feature_service.py) therefore runs immediately BEFORE `to_model_ready` at all three sites that scale — `scale()`, `features(scale=True)`, and `prepare_holdout_for_run` — never after.
decisions.t05_first_open_decision_resolved_neither: D7. Answers T05's own first openDecision: does train.py already drop non-Good FEATURE rows? NO, on either side, and it structurally CANNOT from inside train.py — by the time either frame (train/test or holdout) reaches the trainer, `to_model_ready` has already scaled and Good-stamped every finite cell server-side. `labelled_mask` (D4) only ever excluded non-Good TARGET rows, a different column entirely. This is what makes D6's write-time placement not just cheaper but the ONLY point in the whole pipeline where the distinction still exists.

openDecisions: DOES train.py ALREADY DROP NON-GOOD FEATURE ROWS, OR ONLY NON-GOOD TARGET ROWS? Its own module docstring warns about the ordering of 'the non-Good-target drop', which establishes the target case exists. The feature case is UNVERIFIED. If features are already dropped on the train side, T05 is making the holdout side match. If they are not, this is a gap on BOTH sides today and T05 should not silently fix only one of them — that would make the two scores incomparable in a new way while appearing to fix a problem.

WHERE THE BAD-ROW EXCLUSION HAPPENS: in the holdout write (so validate_data.parquet contains only scoreable rows and its own row count is honest about what will be scored), or at score time in train.py (so the sidecar keeps every holdout row and the exclusion is reported per run). The first is cheaper and makes validationRowCount mean what it says; the second keeps the artifact complete and lets the exclusion rule change without rewriting objects. Not chosen.

tasks.title: Move the split point: _split_holdout runs on the post-features frame
tasks.scope_note:
_split_holdout itself is UNCHANGED — it is a pure timestamp-mask function and knows nothing about which columns the frame carries (DS-LAKE-018-T03/T06 already share it verbatim between materialize and resplit; keep that). What changes is the call site: it moves out of materialize() and into the features stage, operating on the frame apply_features + select_columns just produced.

DROP THE LEAD-IN ON THIS PATH, DELIBERATELY. _split_holdout copies HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN rows ahead of the boundary so a raw holdout can compute its own lag/rolling values. A feature-bearing holdout already has them computed, so lead-in rows would be training rows sitting in the holdout file with no purpose — and they would be SCORED, silently inflating the holdout row count with rows the model trained on. This is the single easiest thing in this task to get wrong by leaving the shared function's default behaviour in place; it must be a parameter, tested both ways, not an assumption.

validationRowCount / validationHoldoutFrom now land on the SILVER row rather than the BRONZE row. claim() (model-run.authorized.service.ts) currently looks up 'the run's GOLD artifact's sibling BRONZE (same wizard runId)' for validationRowCount — that resolver must change. Find every reader of those two columns before changing where they are written.

DONE (2026-08-25). `_split_holdout` gained an optional `lead_in: timedelta = HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN` param (default preserves both existing callers byte-identical). `features()` accepts `request.holdout`: when present, splits AFTER apply_features/select_columns with `lead_in=timedelta(0)`, commits the train side under `target_key`, writes `validate_data.parquet` beside it via the same `sidecar_key` convention `materialize`/`resplit_holdout` use, and returns all three `validation_*` stats through the existing `_commit`/`_stats_payload` plumbing (already carried these fields, no new ones). `FeaturesRequest.holdout: Optional[HoldoutSplitRequest]` added. Threaded through the backend: `CreateFeaturesSchema.holdout` -> `startDraftFeaturesJobService`'s stored job payload -> the runner's `FeatureJobRecipe.holdout` -> the `/v1/preprocess/features` call body -> `commit()` writes `validationRowCount`/`validationHoldoutFrom`/`validationMissingPct` onto the SILVER row. Also wired into the inline `createDraftFeaturesArtifactService` route for parity with the job path (same reasoning DS-LAKE-022 used for `scale`: two call sites that can silently drift). FOUND AND FIXED, same class of bug DS-LAKE-022 hit twice already: the DTO field was built but never forwarded onto the stored payload at the create site — would have left the whole path unreachable. Verified: V01 (real lag/rolling values), V02 (no lead-in leak, both `_split_holdout` lead_in values), V03 (mid-window seam, both the NEW order's correct value and the OLD order's reproduced defect) all pass. Also found and recorded: `validationHoldoutFrom` was written by only 1 of the 3 pre-existing legacy writers (materialize/draft-materialize omit it) — the new SILVER writer does not repeat that gap.

tasks.title: Retain the pre-split SILVER so a holdout change is lossless and idempotent
tasks.scope_note:
Mirror DS-LAKE-018-T06's own structure exactly rather than inventing a second shape: resplit resolves the draft's never-split source by walking UP the parentArtifactId chain, refuses a source that already carries a validationRowCount (it was split, so re-splitting would permanently shed rows), and always writes a NEW artifact. Only the definition of 'pristine' changes — pre-split SILVER instead of pristine BRONZE.

NO RETENTION PIN NEEDED, per the findings: apply_features is deterministic, so pristine SILVER is reproducible from the pinned BRONZE plus the recipe. Confirm that lib/artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts's SILVER handling is unaffected before relying on it — DS-LAKE-018-T06 already checked that this predicate never reads parentArtifactId, so a superseded split-SILVER releases by age like any other intermediate.

DONE (2026-08-25) — verification only, no new code needed. Confirmed the features job always sources the draft's BRONZE (`dwDraftArtifactIdAtom`, read at `use-dataset-gold-warm.ts`), never its own prior SILVER output — re-running on any recipe OR holdout edit is therefore inherently lossless and idempotent for free, with no pristine-walk to build. Confirmed `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts` reads only `{id,type,draftId,createdAt}` (no `parentArtifactId`, no `validationRowCount`) and BRONZE keeps its existing lineage hard-pin while SILVER stays age-releasable — correct, since a superseded split SILVER is fully reproducible from the pinned BRONZE plus the recipe. `resplit_holdout`/`resplitDraftHoldoutService` confirmed byte-unchanged (diffed against the base commit) — edit mode's path is untouched.

tasks.title: Holdout scoring path: scale with recorded params, do not replay
tasks.scope_note:
For a post-reorder dataset the whole path is: read validate_data.parquet -> to_model_ready(frame, tags, scalers, fitted_params=recorded scalingParams) -> score. That is it. to_model_ready already accepts fitted_params (DS-LAKE-018-T02 built exactly this primitive for exactly this reason), so no new transform is written.

SCALING WITH RECORDED PARAMS IS STILL REQUIRED AND IS NOT CLEANING. The model was fitted on scaled values; scoring against unscaled ones would be meaningless. Decision (a) rules out fill/imputation, not the scaler — and the params come from train, never from the holdout's own statistics, which is the whole point of T02.

KEEP THE LEGACY BRANCH. A pre-reorder holdout is raw and still needs replay_holdout_for_run, HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN and max_replay_lookback's refusal. Branch on pipelineVersion (T04), not on inspecting the object's columns — a column-sniffing heuristic would misclassify a legacy holdout of a dataset that happened to have no derived features.

DONE (2026-08-25). New `prepare_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py) + `PrepareHoldoutForRunRequest` schema + `POST /v1/preprocess/prepare-holdout-for-run` route: reads `validate_data.parquet` (already feature-bearing, no lead-in), applies ONLY `to_model_ready(..., fitted_params=scalingParams)` — no apply_features, no select_columns, nothing to trim. Added a coverage guard beyond what `replay_holdout_for_run` has: refuses loudly if any scaled tag (method != 'none') has no recorded `scalingParams` entry, since `to_model_ready`'s per-tag lookup would otherwise silently re-fit that tag on the holdout's own statistics. `model-run.authorized.service.ts`'s `tryReplayHoldout` rewritten per D1: resolves the same-`runId` artifact (BRONZE or SILVER) carrying a non-null `validationRowCount`, DETERMINISTICALLY ordered (`orderBy: {createdAt: 'desc'}` — the pre-existing resolver's own unordered `findFirst` was a real bug this audit found: a multiply-resplit draft can leave two artifacts sharing one runId), then branches on `.type`: BRONZE -> `replayHoldoutForRun` (unchanged), SILVER -> new `prepareHoldoutForRun`. D4 implemented in `images/trainer/train.py`: extracted the existing non-Good-target mask (steps 6-7) into a shared `labelled_mask()` function, applied to BOTH the train/test split (unchanged behaviour, refactor only) AND the holdout scoring block (NEW — previously nothing excluded an unlabelled holdout row, so a sparse lab target likely produced NaN in r2_score and silently swallowed holdout metrics entirely via the surrounding best-effort except). `holdoutMetrics.dropped_unlabelled` now reported alongside row_count. New test coverage: 5 python tests for prepare_holdout_for_run, 2 new + 1 fixed backend model-run spec tests (the pre-existing fixture never set `type: 'BRONZE'`, so it silently exercised the wrong branch once the two-branch resolver existed), 4 new standalone tests for `labelled_mask` (images/trainer had zero test infrastructure before this).

tasks.title: pipelineVersion becomes a correctness dependency, not a diagnostic
tasks.scope_note:
DS-LAKE-022-T03 proposes DatasetArtifact.pipelineVersion Int? (null = pre-reorder) for readability. This feature makes it load-bearing: claim() cannot choose between T03's two branches without it, and choosing wrong is not a cosmetic error — replaying a recipe onto a frame that already has the derived columns hits apply_features' own name-collision skip and produces a holdout that looks fine and was never actually transformed.

The two features must agree on one column, not add two. If DS-LAKE-022-T03 lands first, use its column; if this feature lands first, DS-LAKE-022-T03 consumes it. Whichever order, the value must be written by the stage that produces the artifact, not backfilled by a reader.

DONE (2026-08-25) — decision only, implemented as part of T03. D1: the discriminator is WHICH ARTIFACT ROW carries `validationRowCount` (BRONZE = legacy raw = replay; SILVER = feature-bearing = prepare), not `pipelineVersion` as originally proposed. Rejected because DS-LAKE-022 already stamps `pipelineVersion: 2` on every create-mode SILVER regardless of whether a holdout was ever picked — branching on it alone would send an ordinary reordered-wizard dataset (features-only SILVER, holdout still raw at BRONZE from before DS-LAKE-023 or from edit mode) down the wrong (SILVER/prepare) branch and try to score a raw holdout as if it already had features. No schema change; `pipelineVersion` stays a diagnostic, as originally intended.

tasks.title: Exclude unscoreable holdout rows, and report how many
tasks.scope_note:
BLOCKED ON openDecisions — both of them. Answer whether train.py already drops non-Good feature rows before deciding what 'match the train side' means, and decide whether exclusion happens at write time or at score time.

What is NOT in question is that something must happen: per the findings, a Bad derived cell is stored as 0.0, to_model_ready scales it and stamps it Good, and the model predicts from a fabricated zero. A rolling(60) column turns one short dropout into sixty such rows.

Exclusion is row-level and status-driven, so it needs no statistic from the train side and does not violate decision (a). REPORT THE COUNT ALONGSIDE THE HOLDOUT METRICS, for the reason DS-LAKE-010-T06 and DS-LAKE-018 both already state about missing rates: a score computed over an unstated subset is not comparable to anything. Publish it beside the metric the way MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 requires for the holdout's own missing rate.

DEFERRED (2026-08-25), per explicit user scope decision for this session's pass (T01-T04+T06 only). D5 resolves this task's FIRST openDecision: exclusion must apply to BOTH the train/test split AND the holdout, with counts reported on both sides — fixing only the holdout side (as this task's own scope_note originally leaned toward) would make the two scores incomparable in a NEW way while looking like a fix, which is the exact risk this task's own second finding named. The second openDecision (exclude at write time vs score time) stays genuinely open — undecided because unbuilt, not overlooked. Adjacent to, and NOT satisfied by, D4 (T03): D4 excludes non-Good TARGET rows from holdout scoring; T05 is about non-Good FEATURE rows (a Bad derived cell stored as 0.0, scaled, stamped Good) — the two are different failure modes on different columns.

IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-26), per D6/D7 above (write-time, both sides). `drop_bad_feature_rows(frame, tags, exclude=target_y)` (feature_service.py) — pure, drops any row where a KEPT tag's own status column is not STATUS_GOOD, `target_y` exempted (D4's own labelled_mask concern, not this function's). Wired immediately before `to_model_ready` at all three scaling sites: `scale()`, `features(scale=True)` (train side only — `validate_frame`, if present, is untouched here; it stays raw until `prepare_holdout_for_run` runs its OWN call right before ITS `to_model_ready`, which is the actual pre-scale point for the holdout side), and `prepare_holdout_for_run`. Count threaded end-to-end as `dropped_bad_rows`/`droppedBadRows`/`dropped_bad_features`: `_stats_payload`/`_commit` (python) -> `ArtifactStatsResponse` (FastAPI response_model — declared explicitly, not left to the same silent-strip bug `validation_missing_pct`'s own comment records) -> `ArtifactStatsSchema` (NestJS zod) -> `DatasetArtifact.droppedBadRows Int?` (new column, `db push`'d — see this session's own migration-drift note) written by `preprocessing-job.service.ts`'s commit block and `createDraftFeaturesArtifactService` -> for the holdout side specifically, `ReplayHoldoutForRunSchema.dropped_bad_rows` -> `tryReplayHoldout`'s new `holdoutDroppedBadRows` field (captured from `prepareHoldoutForRun`'s own return value, which the pre-existing code discarded entirely) -> `claim()`'s response (already spreads `...(holdout ?? {})`, no change needed there) -> `train.py`'s `holdout_metrics.dropped_bad_features`. NOT DONE: V05 itself (a live dropout-window test proving the exclusion actually fires and is counted, not scored as scaled zeros) — status stays in_progress, not completed, until that test exists and passes.

V05 PROVEN (2026-08-26) — see its own note. Correcting the 5 pre-existing tests this fix's row-count/scaling-value change broke was part of finishing this task, not separate scope: test_features_writes_the_real_fitted_scaling_params, test_features_formula_kind_is_computed, test_features_scale_true_default_is_byte_identical_to_before_the_split, test_scale_writes_feature_spec_and_forces_good, and test_reorder_v04_scaling_params_differ_between_old_and_new_order (this last one needed a real behavioural addition, not just a number change — T05 fixes the SAME Bad-row defect the V04 reorder test was built to demonstrate, on BOTH the old and new pipeline order alike, so its own new_store gained a genuine `clip` cleaning op to keep proving the reorder itself still matters for a value T05 does not already handle). Full python suite: 756 passed, 74 skipped (live-infra tests, unrelated), 0 failed.

tasks.title: Step 4 UI: pick the holdout after Apply Feature, and state the ordering constraint
tasks.scope_note:
Mount the SAME ValidationHoldoutSection component (DS-LAKE-018-T06 already extracted it out of step-2-raw-data.tsx into processing/validation-holdout-section.tsx for exactly this kind of move), below the feature list, enabled only once a feature artifact exists.

THE NEW CONSTRAINT MUST BE VISIBLE, because it did not exist before and nothing else can express it: editing a feature config after the holdout is cut invalidates the holdout, since the sidecar's own bytes carry the derived columns. Either re-split automatically on a recipe change (the resplit machinery from T02 makes this cheap) or disable the recipe editors once a holdout exists — the first is friendlier and the second is more honest; not chosen here.

The four guards from DS-LAKE-018-T01's describeHoldoutSelection carry over unchanged, with one becoming more accurate and one becoming less relevant: the containment and remaining-labelled-rows guards are unaffected; guard 4 (trailing recommended) now warns about the training DISTRIBUTION rather than about wrong feature values, since the seam no longer corrupts derived columns; guard 3 (lead-in availability) no longer applies at all on this path and must not fire, or it will refuse a perfectly valid selection for a reason that no longer exists.

DONE (2026-08-25). `ValidationHoldoutSection` moved from `processing/step-3-1-EDA.tsx` to `step-4-feature-engineering.tsx`, mounted below the feature tabs/DataAnalysisCard. `useDatasetGoldWarm` gained a 5th arg (`holdout?: {from,to}|null`), forwarded into the job payload ONLY when `isReordered` (create mode) — added to Step 4's warm effect's dependency array alongside the feature recipe, so a holdout edit and a recipe edit both re-fire the SAME debounced warm rather than racing. This is what makes 'auto re-split on recipe change' (D3, this feature's own resolution of DS-LAKE-022-T06's unresolved question) fall out for free — no new resplit mechanism, just one more dependency on an already-debounced effect. Edit mode's `useDatasetHoldoutResplit()` is called UNCONDITIONALLY (Rules of Hooks) but its real result is only wired to the section in edit mode; create mode gets a stable, module-scope no-op result object instead, since the atom write `ValidationHoldoutSection` already makes is sufficient there. `describeHoldoutSelection` (lib/holdout.ts) gained `featureBearing?: boolean` (default false): guard 3 (lead-in availability) is skipped entirely when true (a feature-bearing split trims lead-in to zero server-side, so there is nothing to be short of); guard 4 (trailing recommended) branches its message — the old 'reads rows from the wrong side of it' claim is now FALSE for a feature-bearing split (features compute on the continuous frame before the cut), reworded to warn about the training DISTRIBUTION instead. `ValidationHoldoutSection` forwards `featureBearing={!nav.isEditLocked}` from its new Step 4 mount. Also fixed the two stale comments the audit found: `holdout.ts`'s own doc block still said 'Step 2' and claimed the target is set at 'Step 4' when its only writer is Step 1 (`unified-tag-table.tsx`); `wizard-shell.tsx` still said 'five steps'; `use-dataset-gold-warm.ts` still referenced the pre-rename `step-5-review-save.tsx`. Verified: tsc 0 errors, 11/11 gold-warm tests (2 new for holdout forwarding), full client vitest run shows the SAME 8 pre-existing failing files confirmed unrelated last session (useAtom, use-plants-data, plans, step-6-review-save x2, isometric-map, machine-node, use-dashboard-data, canvas-page) — no new failures.

tasks.scope_note:
Add ONE superseded_by note to DS-LAKE-018 naming exactly which of its parts this feature replaces for new datasets and which remain live for existing ones: split point (moved), HOLDOUT_LEAD_IN and max_replay_lookback and replay_holdout's refusal (legacy path only), replay_holdout / replay_holdout_for_run (legacy path only), scalingParams (unchanged and now the ONLY remaining transform-transfer mechanism, so more load-bearing than before), the resolved no-imputation decision (unchanged, and it is what answers this feature's own cleaning question), resplit_holdout (mechanism unchanged, 'pristine' redefined).
