tasks.title: Edit-mode holdout re-split: give the features job a correctly-cleaned source
tasks.scope_note: [unchanged — kept verbatim as the record of what was believed at the time]
tasks.result:
SUPERSEDED BY DS-LAKE-024, NOT BUILT. DS-LAKE-023's decision D2 (create_mode_only) carries an explicit escape clause — 'until/unless a future feature unlocks edit-mode feature editing, at which point this decision should be revisited'. DS-LAKE-024 ('Edit mode gets a DatasetDraft') is that feature.

WHY OPTION (a) BECOMES UNNECESSARY, STATED CORRECTLY. This task's premise was that features must NOT source BRONZE, because edit mode's order was BRONZE -> clean -> features+scale and sourcing BRONZE would silently skip cleaning. That premise was true under the pre-DS-LAKE-022 order and is FALSE under it: 022 moves cleaning to operate on the FEATURE artifact, so the shared order becomes BRONZE -> features -> clean -> scale. features-from-BRONZE is therefore correct because THE ORDER CHANGED, not because edit mode now matches the old order. Do not read this closure as endorsing the order quoted in the scope_note above — implementing to that string reproduces the exact regression this task's own findings caught mid-session ('UNIFYING EDIT MODE... REVERTED MID-SESSION').

So option (a) — walk currentArtifact.parentArtifactId back to the pre-features cleaned intermediate of the original run and adopt it into a fresh draft — is not needed: the edit draft is rooted at the adopted BRONZE (DS-LAKE-024 decisions.seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_refetch) and produces its own cleaned artifact in-session through the existing draft-scoped clean path. No adoption of an artifact belonging to an older run's pipeline stage, and no fallback needed for the reclaimed-intermediate case that made (a) genuinely new backend work.

OPEN QUESTION THIS CLOSURE DOES NOT SETTLE: under the 022 order, cleaning is DOWNSTREAM of features, so the holdout section may no longer need a cleaned source at all — in which case this task is not superseded but DISSOLVED, its premise gone rather than satisfied elsewhere. The distinction matters for whether DS-LAKE-024-T04 inherits a cleaned-source precondition or none. Recorded here, decided in 022.

CORRECTION TO OPTION (b), WITH THE DEFECT SPUN OUT. The scope_note claimed (b) needs 'NO further code, only a decision', because visiting Step 5 and running Save Cleaned Tags once — even with zero rules — would advance dwDraftArtifactIdAtom 'for free'. FALSE, and verified: dataset-draft-pipeline.ts:198 early-returns from applyClean when steps.length === 0, and step-5-data-cleaning.tsx:226 only calls applyClean when draft.length > 0. A user who wants zero cleaning rules can never advance the atom past null through Step 5 at all. (b) was never free.

That defect is NOT DS-LAKE-024's to fix — none of its seven tasks touch the clean pipeline, and the boundary belongs to use-dataset-draft-pipeline.ts. Spun out as DS-LAKE-022-T0N (see below) rather than left as a sentence in a closed task's result.

THE ORIGINAL REQUEST REMAINS PARTLY OPEN. The scope_note's own closing line — edit mode should be re-splittable independent of a Step 5 visit — is satisfied by DS-LAKE-024 only for datasets whose adopted root BRONZE is pristine. Per DS-LAKE-024-T04 and decisions.resplit_is_offered_only_when_it_can_succeed, a pre-DS-LAKE-018-T06 dataset gets a DISABLED picker naming re-fetch as the way forward. So 'edit mode is re-splittable' is true for post-T06 datasets and false for older ones, and DS-LAKE-024-T01's second read is what says how many datasets fall on each side. This task closes; that gap does not.

TERMINOLOGY HAZARD, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: 'SILVER' means the CLEANED artifact in this ledger and the FEATURE artifact in DS-LAKE-022/024. One of the two must be renamed before either ledger is read by anyone who did not write it. Not done here — a rename touching two ledgers is its own change, not a footnote in a closure.

acceptance_criteria: validate_data.parquet contains the derived feature columns and their computed values, for a dataset whose holdout was picked at the Feature Engineering step.
It contains NO lead-in rows — every row in it is inside the chosen holdout window.
The holdout rows are absent from the train frame and therefore from cleaning, from GOLD, from FINAL and from training.
A derived value in the holdout equals the value the same recipe would produce on the continuous frame — no boundary artefact at the split.
A derived value in the TRAIN frame equally has no boundary artefact, even for a mid-window holdout — the seam fix, verified rather than assumed.
The holdout is scaled with the train's recorded scalingParams and never re-fit on itself.
The holdout is never cleaned or imputed; unscoreable rows are excluded and the excluded count is reported beside the holdout metrics.
A dataset whose holdout predates this feature still scores, via the retained replay path, chosen by pipelineVersion rather than by inspecting the object.
Changing a feature config after a holdout is cut cannot leave a holdout describing a recipe that no longer exists.
No existing object is renamed, moved or rewritten.

verification.description: PROVE THE HOLDOUT CARRIES REAL FEATURE VALUES, NOT JUST FEATURE COLUMNS: pick a holdout on a recipe with a lag(5) and a rolling(60), and assert the holdout's FIRST row has a real value for both — and that it equals the value computed on the continuous pre-split frame at that same timestamp. Asserting the columns merely EXIST would pass against a split that produced them all-Bad, which is the failure the old lead-in mechanism existed to prevent and which this design is supposed to make impossible.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-25): test_features_holdout_v01_carries_real_computed_feature_values — day15's lag5 (10.0) and roll6_mean (12.5) both match the continuous 20-day frame's own values at that timestamp, not a placeholder or all-Bad column.

verification.description: PROVE NO LEAD-IN ROWS LEAKED IN: assert every timestamp in validate_data.parquet falls inside the chosen window. _split_holdout is shared with the legacy path and copies lead-in rows by default, so a forgotten parameter here silently puts training rows into the scored set and inflates the row count with rows the model already saw — a difference a row-count assertion alone would read as plausible.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-25): test_features_holdout_v02_no_lead_in_rows_leak_into_validate — every validate_data.parquet timestamp is >= the holdout start (5 rows, not 12), AND `_split_holdout` directly asserts 12 rows at the default lead-in vs 5 at lead_in=timedelta(0), pinning the exact difference a forgotten parameter would have caused.

verification.description: PROVE THE SEAM FIX IS REAL, BOTH SIDES: cut a MID-WINDOW holdout and assert that the train frame's first row after the cut has a lag value equal to what the continuous frame produced there. Under the old order that value read across the gap from the wrong side. A trailing holdout cannot distinguish the fixed behaviour from the broken one, so the mid-window case is the only one that tests this.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-25): test_features_holdout_v03_mid_window_seam_has_no_boundary_artifact — a day10-12 holdout's first train row after the cut (day13) reads lag1=12.0 under the NEW order (features on the continuous frame first) versus the OLD order's own reproduced defect (9.0, reading across the reindexed gap), proven by running BOTH orders against the same source frame in one test.

verification.description: PROVE SCALING STILL USES THE TRAIN'S PARAMS: score the same holdout once with the recorded scalingParams and once re-fitting on the holdout itself, and assert the results DIFFER — DS-LAKE-018-V02's own construction, re-run one layer up now that replay no longer sits between them. If they agree the params are being ignored and nothing else in this feature would reveal it.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-25): test_prepare_scales_with_recorded_params_not_a_fresh_fit (day7-9 scaled to [0.07,0.08,0.09] via recorded min=0/max=100, not re-fit to the holdout's own [7,9] range) plus test_prepare_refuses_a_scaled_tag_with_no_recorded_params, the NEW coverage guard beyond what this verification originally asked for.

verification.description: PROVE THE BAD-CELL PATH IS HANDLED: build a holdout window containing a sensor dropout long enough to make a rolling(60) column Bad, and confirm those rows are excluded and counted — not scored as scaled zeros. A holdout with clean data cannot distinguish a working exclusion from none, and the scaled-zero path returns a plausible number rather than an error.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-26): test_prepare_excludes_bad_feature_rows_instead_of_scoring_scaled_zeros (test_artifact_service_prepare_holdout.py, holdout side) and its TRAIN-side mirror test_scale_excludes_bad_feature_rows_instead_of_scoring_scaled_zeros (test_artifact_service_features.py) — a 6-row fixture with a roll60_mean column Bad on exactly 2 rows (simulating a rolling(60) window straddling a sensor dropout, without needing 60 real rows). Both prove: dropped_bad_rows==2, the written frame keeps only the 4 surviving rows (asserted by exact surviving timestamps, not just a row count), and the surviving rows' status is genuinely Good post-scale — not a laundered Bad-cell 0.0. Also reused every existing test in this file/test_artifact_service_features.py; 5 of those needed correcting (see T05's own scope_note) because they had encoded the PRE-fix Bad-row-laundering behaviour as expected.

verification.description: PROVE THE LEGACY PATH STILL WORKS: score a dataset whose validate_data.parquet is raw and predates this feature, and confirm it goes through replay with its lead-in and lookback checks intact. Testing only new datasets would leave every existing saved dataset silently unscoreable.
verification.note: PROVEN (2026-08-25) via the model-run.authorized.service.spec.ts fixture fix + its pre-existing passing tests: a BRONZE-type holdout artifact (type:'BRONZE', the legacy fixture's default) routes to replayHoldoutForRun unchanged, with holdout_from forwarded. The SILVER-branch test added alongside it (routes to prepareHoldoutForRun instead) is the direct proof the two are mutually exclusive per D1.

verification.description: Change a feature config after cutting a holdout and confirm the holdout cannot remain stale — either it re-splits or the edit is refused. A holdout whose bytes describe a recipe that no longer exists is the one failure mode this design introduces that the old one could not have.
verification.note:
SATISFIED BY DESIGN, not a dedicated test (2026-08-25): D3 makes a stale holdout structurally impossible in create mode rather than something to detect after the fact — `dwHoldoutRangeAtom` is a dependency of the SAME debounced warm effect the feature recipe already re-fires on, so a feature-config edit and a holdout edit are the same code path, not two that could get out of sync. Editing the recipe re-derives Step 4's SILVER AND (if a holdout is set) re-splits it in one job call — there is no separate 'stale holdout' state to reach.

COMPLETED BY A SEPARATE GUARANTEE (2026-08-26), same status kept (this claim was true, just incomplete): the paragraph above proves a stale holdout cannot exist at the JOB-CALL level (one warm call, one bundled recipe). It does not by itself prove Step 5 can never CONSUME an artifact from a call that predates the user's latest edit — `goTo` (the step indicator) never called `canAdvance`, so a holdout Applied then immediately followed by a jump to Step 5 could reach `useDatasetCleaningScaleCommit` before the warm this Apply scheduled had landed, committing the PREVIOUS artifact with no error. Closed by a second, independent check inside `commit()` itself: it refuses unless `dwFeatureWarmStateAtom==='ready'` AND `dwFeatureArtifactStampAtom` (the committed artifact's own recipe signature) matches the CURRENT recipe's signature, computed the same way (`featureRecipeStamp`). This is what makes V07's own claim true of what Step 5 actually commits, not only of what Step 4 calls.

features.title: Edit mode gets a DatasetDraft, and Save writes a new VERSION of the existing Dataset
features.description: Opening a saved dataset in Edit seeds a DatasetDraft from its adopted BRONZE, so every draft-scoped endpoint the wizard already has works unchanged — features, holdout resplit, cleaning jobs, chart tabs. Save from edit mode then writes a NEW DatasetVersion of the SAME Dataset instead of a new Dataset row.
findings: EVERY PROCESSING ENDPOINT IS DRAFT-SCOPED, AND TWO HAVE NO DATASET-SCOPED TWIN AT ALL. createDraftFeaturesArtifactService and resplitDraftHoldoutService exist only on authorized/dataset-drafts. /clean, /job, /retry, /rows, /metadata, /tags and /column-stats each have a dataset-scoped sibling; /features and /holdout do not. GREP TO CONFIRM before building — this is inferred from the ledger's own silence, and silence is not evidence. DS-LAKE-005B-D-T05 recorded the identical shape once already for the chart endpoints ('have no dataset-scoped (non-draft) twin; adding one is out of scope here'), so the pattern is established, not novel.

EDIT MODE IS A RECIPE-METADATA EDITOR TODAY, NOT A RE-PROCESSING FLOW — WHICH IS WHY THE TWO SYMPTOMS ARE ONE CAUSE. DS-LAKE-009-V01 grepped every prisma.datasetVersion.create call site and found exactly ONE, inside saveDraftAsDatasetService. So edit mode cannot produce a new version, therefore cannot produce a new artifact, therefore cannot add a feature or re-split a holdout. 'Add a feature' and 'resplit the holdout' are not two bugs; they are one missing capability seen from two angles.

HALF OF THIS IS A RECORDED DECISION, BUT ITS STATED REASON MAY NO LONGER HOLD. DS-LAKE-018-T01 says: 'edit mode's picker is disabled since BRONZE is already split by the time a recipe is editable.' That was true when the picker lived at Step 2 and materialize() cut the holdout inline. DS-LAKE-018-T06 then moved the picker to Step 3.1, so dwHoldoutRangeAtom is null during Step 2's background warm, materialize runs WITHOUT a holdout, and resplit writes a split CHILD of a pristine root. DS-LAKE-017-T01 adopts lineage[0] — the parentArtifactId: null root — so for a post-T06 dataset the adopted BRONZE is PRISTINE and re-splittable. For a pre-T06 dataset it is not. The same feature therefore has two different truths depending on when the dataset was created, and neither the UI nor the ledger currently distinguishes them.

PRE-T06 DATASETS ALSO HYDRATE AN INCOMPLETE FRAME, AND NOTHING SAYS SO. Where materialize() cut the holdout inline, the adopted BRONZE's data.parquet is the TRAIN side only. Edit mode hydrating it shows fewer rows than the user fetched at Step 2, with no explanation — and wizard-shell's showStageWarning stays silent, because the stage genuinely IS BRONZE. The user reads 'normal'. Not introduced by this feature; made visible by it, because a draft seeded from that artifact inherits the gap.

GIVING EDIT MODE A DRAFT ALSO ARMS CONTROLS THAT WERE DELIBERATELY INERT. dwHoldoutRangeAtom already has an edit-mode hydration branch (config.holdoutDateRange ?? null) written as display-only. With a draft present the picker becomes live — and on a pre-T06 dataset resplit_holdout refuses with 422 ('re-splitting an ALREADY-split frame would permanently shed rows'). A clickable control that fails is worse than a disabled one, which is DS-LAKE-010-T08's own reasoning about a Resume button that typechecked and did nothing.

savedDatasetId CANNOT SIMPLY BE REUSED — IT WOULD CARRY TWO MEANINGS ON ONE COLUMN. Today it is written at Save and means 'this draft BECAME that Dataset' (an outcome). Edit mode needs 'this draft is EDITING that Dataset' (an origin), written at creation. Overloading it makes 'is this draft saved?' unanswerable from the row alone, and DatasetDraft.status already carries SAVED — so the two would have to be read together to mean anything. An earlier framing of this feature claimed the column could be reused as-is; that was wrong and is corrected here.

SAVE-AS-NEW-VERSION IS A DECOMPOSITION, NOT A REUSE. saveDraftAsDatasetService does five things in one transaction: create the Dataset, adopt FINAL, adopt the lineage-root BRONZE (DS-LAKE-017-T01), create the DatasetVersion, and flip the draft to SAVED. Edit mode needs the last four with the first replaced by 'resolve the existing Dataset'. The versionNumber allocation is genuinely reusable (DS-LAKE-009-T03 reads max inside the transaction so concurrent saves cannot collide on @@unique([datasetId, versionNumber])), as is the LoaderJob enqueue-after-transaction ordering (DS-LAKE-011-T03). An earlier framing called this 'the only new thing, and the mechanism already exists' — the mechanism exists, the decomposition does not.

DS-LAKE-022 AND -023 WIDEN THIS GAP RATHER THAN NARROWING IT. Under 022 cleaning operates on the SILVER (feature) artifact — an edit-mode session with no draft has no SILVER, so the new Step 5 would have nothing to clean. Under 023 the holdout is cut after apply_features, so 'cannot add a feature' becomes 'cannot resplit' by construction. And pipelineVersion means an edited dataset must know which pipeline order produced it before replaying anything. All three land on the same missing piece.

THE PRECEDENT FOR THIS FEATURE IS THE PROJECT'S OWN draft_first DECISION, APPLIED ONE CASE FURTHER. decisions.draft_first: 'A dedicated DatasetDraft entity owns wizard-time artifacts and jobs... the draft is what makes that possible without an orphan Dataset row.' An edit session IS a wizard run — same five (soon six) steps, same async jobs, same need for artifacts that must not become the live dataset until Save. It was left out because at the time edit mode changed nothing but metadata.

UPDATE (T00): zero instances today. All 5 adopted root BRONZE rows are pristine (validationRowCount null), so every existing dataset falls on the post-T06 side. The two-truths problem is real and producible (939862b0's lineage carries a resplit child) but no current dataset is on the pre-T06 side of it.
UPDATE (T00): zero instances today, same census as finding 3 — no adopted root is a train-side-only frame. Retained because the shape is producible, not because a dataset exhibits it.

edit_mode_gets_a_draft.chosen: Seed a DatasetDraft on entering edit mode, rather than building dataset-scoped twins of /features and /holdout
edit_mode_gets_a_draft.rationale: Four endpoints, both chart-tab surfaces, the readiness caption and the whole job-polling path already work against a draft and need no change. The twin approach duplicates that surface and still leaves the real gap open — an artifact produced by a dataset-scoped /features would have no DatasetVersion pointing at it, which is the same orphan shape draft_first exists to prevent.

rejected.Dataset-scoped /features and /holdout tw: Duplicates a working surface, and does not produce a version. Two implementations of the same processing step is how they diverge — the reason DS-LAKE-003 killed the three-way key-template drift and DS-LAKE-021-T02's poller was generalised rather than copied.
rejected.Reuse savedDatasetId for the origin poin: See findings — two meanings on one column, and status already carries the outcome half.

origin_is_its_own_column.chosen: DatasetDraft.editingDatasetId String? — null for a create-mode draft
origin_is_its_own_column.rationale: Origin and outcome are different facts about different moments, exactly as DatasetArtifact keeps draftId (origin) alongside datasetId (adoption) rather than moving one into the other — DS-LAKE-004B's both_set_is_legal is the same shape. Nullable and additive, so every existing draft row and every existing reader is unaffected.
origin_is_its_own_column.consequence: Save branches on it: null takes today's create-a-Dataset path unchanged, non-null takes the new version path. One branch, read from a row, rather than a client-supplied mode flag the server would have to trust.

seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_r.chosen: The edit draft points at the existing adopted BRONZE artifact; it does not re-materialize from the source
seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_r.rationale: DS-LAKE-017 exists so edit mode reads raw instead of re-cleaning FINAL. Re-fetching would cost minutes, could return different rows (a PI archive absorbs backfills, per decisions.reproducibility_anchor), and would make an edit session non-reproducible against the version it started from. T00 read 4 adds a second, stronger reason: the intermediate artifacts a re-processing edit mode might otherwise root at are NOT retained — 0 of 7 SILVER and 0 of 33 GOLD are adopted, 3 SILVER and 28 GOLD already carry objectReclaimedAt, and 2 of 5 saved lineages contain no SILVER link at all. The adopted BRONZE is the only root that exists for every saved dataset.
seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_r.correction: THIS DECISION'S ORIGINAL RATIONALE WAS WRONG ABOUT WHY THE BYTES SURVIVE. It claimed artifact-cleanup-eligibility 'hard-pins a BRONZE reachable through a non-ARCHIVED DatasetVersion's parentArtifactId chain regardless of age'. T00 read 4 found :275 releases SILVER/GOLD BY AGE ALONE WHILE STILL LINEAGE-REACHABLE — so lineage-reachability is not the retention mechanism for intermediates. The 5 adopted BRONZE rows are intact, but the audit did not establish WHY: adoption (datasetId non-null) is the likely mechanism, not reachability. Whether adoption actually exempts a row from age-release is UNVERIFIED and is T01's third read. The conclusion stands on the census; the mechanism does not stand on anything yet.
seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_r.consequence: The draft's own artifact chain starts from an artifact whose draftId belongs to a DIFFERENT, older draft. Legal (DatasetArtifact carries both owners and the CHECK only forbids neither) but the edit draft does not OWN its root — cleanup must not treat that root as this draft's to reclaim (T05). If T01's third read finds adoption does NOT exempt from age-release, this decision does not merely need a new rationale: it needs re-deciding, because there would be no retention guarantee for any root at all.

resplit_is_offered_only_when_it_can_succ.chosen: The holdout picker is enabled in edit mode only when the adopted root BRONZE is pristine; otherwise it is disabled with the reason stated
resplit_is_offered_only_when_it_can_succ.rationale: resplit_holdout's 422 is correct and must not be softened — re-splitting an already-split frame permanently sheds rows. What must change is offering the action at all. The row already carries the answer: validationRowCount non-null means the root was split at materialize time. Same discipline as DS-LAKE-020-T05's unit-gate, which disables a toggle and states why rather than letting it fail on click.
resplit_is_offered_only_when_it_can_succ.consequence: A pre-DS-LAKE-018-T06 dataset gets a disabled picker naming re-fetch as the way forward. A post-T06 dataset gets a working one. The UI states which case it is in rather than leaving the user to discover it.

openDecisions: WHAT HAPPENS TO A PREVIOUS VERSION'S ARTIFACTS WHEN A NEW ONE IS SAVED. The old FINAL is still referenced by the old DatasetVersion, so it is lineage-pinned and must survive (DS-LAKE-009B-T08). But Dataset.currentArtifactId and currentVersionId move to the new one, and the old version's status is untouched — so a dataset accumulates ACTIVE-eligible versions with no supersession. DS-LAKE-010-T05 enforces at most one ACTIVE version and deliberately does NOT auto-demote ('the caller demotes the old version first, as its own separate, auditable step'). Whether an edit-save should demote, or leave both at DRAFT, or refuse until the caller demotes, is not decided.

WHETHER AN ABANDONED EDIT DRAFT IS RECLAIMED ON THE SAME WINDOW AS A CREATE DRAFT. DS-LAKE-014's tiers measure from draft.updatedAt and branch on whether the draft owns artifacts. An edit draft owns none at creation (its root belongs to an older draft), so it looks exactly like an empty ACTIVE draft and would be auto-ABANDONED after CLEANUP_ACTIVE_EMPTY_MINUTES (15). That may be right — nothing was computed — but it means opening Edit and leaving the tab for twenty minutes silently abandons the session. Not decided; T05 must at minimum not reclaim the borrowed root either way.

WHETHER EDIT MODE MAY CHANGE THE TAG SET OR ONLY THE RECIPE. Adding a tag needs rows that were never fetched, so it needs a re-materialize — which decisions.seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_refetch rules out for this feature. Removing a tag is just column selection and works today. The boundary should be stated in the UI rather than discovered as a failure.

RESOLVED (DS-LAKE-024-T08): the ROWS path owns root creation (`useDatasetVersionRows` branch 2 already materializes V1 from the saved recipe on Edit-open); the draft resolves AFTER it, via a retry keyed on the rows settling onto a real artifact; and Edit now STATES that there is no raw data instead of leaving it to be inferred. No create-on-enter materialize was added — that would have been the second minting path this decision warned about. Original text follows. --- OPENING EDIT ON A DATASET WITH NO ADOPTED BRONZE. `asd` (8b1c1d53) has currentArtifactId null and zero versions, so T02's 'point currentArtifactId at the adopted BRONZE' has nothing to point at. And T00 read 2 found a second minting path already live: step-6-review-save.tsx:417 calls storeRows(res.data.id, pipelineConfig) when !res.data.currentArtifactId, so an edit-SAVE already mints a BRONZE for exactly this case. Two paths would then mint a root for the same dataset — create-on-enter and save. Decide which owns it: refuse Edit until the dataset has an artifact, have create-on-enter materialize one, or keep the save-time path and have the draft start rootless. Not decided.

THE TAG SET IS ALREADY EDITABLE, AND ALREADY DIVERGES. T00 read 2: updateDatasetService persists `tags` without touching any artifact, so dataset.tags can already name a column no artifact contains — visible today as an all-em-dash row in the detail sheet's per-tag table, because perTagStatsOrdered orders by the DATASET's tag list and finds no sidecar entry. openDecisions[2] and T07 both frame this as a risk this feature would introduce; it is a current-state defect this feature makes reachable from a second surface. Decide whether 024 states the boundary (T07), fixes the divergence, or refuses tag edits outright.

tasks.title: Audit what edit mode already does before rescoping anything
tasks.scope_note:
PREMISE UNDER TEST: that a clean-only edit mode was already built once, worked, and was only abandoned because features could not be added. If true, rescoping 024 to clean-only is a restoration. If false, it is a NEW design that happens to resemble an earlier intention — and must be built, not restored. The ledger's own finding 2 predicts FALSE (one datasetVersion.create call site, inside saveDraftAsDatasetService), so this audit is expected to disconfirm the premise, not confirm it. Report what is found either way.

SEVEN READS, all cheap:

(1) DID EDIT MODE EVER PRODUCE A VERSION? Grep every prisma.datasetVersion.create call site and every caller of saveDraftAsDatasetService. If the only path runs through create-mode Save, then edit mode has never written a version and 'rollback' restores a metadata editor, not a clean-only pipeline. This single read decides whether the rest of this rescope is restoration or construction.

(2) WHAT DOES EDIT MODE PERSIST TODAY? Read use-dataset-edit-hydration and whatever handles edit-mode Save. Enumerate exactly which fields a saved edit writes — name, description, tags, cleaning rules, recipe JSON — and whether any of it touches an artifact. 'Recipe-metadata editor' is the ledger's claim; confirm the boundary rather than inheriting the phrase.

(3) WHAT LANDED IN 023-T08's SESSION, AND IS IT STILL THERE? T08's scope_note says a disabled gate `mode==='edit' && !sourceArtifactId` landed on Step 4's holdout section (D6's fix). Confirm it exists. Under a clean-only rescope the holdout section should not render in edit mode at all, so this gate becomes dead code — note it for removal rather than leaving a disabled control explaining a capability that no longer exists.

(4) IS THE FEATURE ARTIFACT PINNED? saveDraftAsDatasetService adopts FINAL and the lineage-root BRONZE (DS-LAKE-017-T01). Check whether the intermediate feature artifact is adopted, or left owned by the draft and therefore reclaimable. A clean-only edit mode needs that artifact as its ROOT, so if it is unpinned, clean-only edit is impossible without either pinning it or replaying features from BRONZE. This is the same reclaimed-intermediate problem 023-T08 option (a) hit; a clean-only rescope inherits it rather than escaping it.

(5) DOES CLEANING SEE ACROSS THE HOLDOUT BOUNDARY? Under DS-LAKE-023 the holdout is cut after apply_features, so the feature artifact holds train and validation in one frame. Read the imputation and scaling code paths and determine whether either fits statistics on the whole frame. If yes, validation leaks into train — and under a clean-only rescope that leak is present in EVERY edit session rather than some, because cleaning becomes the only thing edit mode does. Highest-severity read here; report the answer explicitly even if it is 'no leak'.

(6) WHAT DOES 'SILVER' MEAN IN THE CODE, not in the ledgers? DS-LAKE-023 uses SILVER for the CLEANED artifact; 022/024 use it for the FEATURE artifact. Grep the enum or string literals and report which the code actually stores. 'Edit from SILVER' is unactionable until this is settled — under one reading it means re-cleaning already-cleaned data.

(7) DOES ANY PRE-022 DATASET HAVE A FEATURES-BEFORE-CLEAN ARTIFACT AT ALL? If the pre-022 order was BRONZE -> clean -> features, then no such artifact exists in that lineage and clean-only edit is UNDEFINED for those datasets — they would need a features replay from BRONZE under the new order. Query how many existing datasets fall on each side of the 022 pipelineVersion boundary; that count decides whether this is an edge case or the majority.

Write all seven answers into this task's result. MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code; a rescope built on an unverified memory of what was built before is the same failure with a different cause.
tasks.result:
PREMISE DISCONFIRMED, AS PREDICTED. Edit mode has never produced a DatasetVersion, so rescoping 024 to clean-only is CONSTRUCTION, not restoration. All seven reads are answered below; reads 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7 are backed by grep plus a live query against local Postgres (soft_sensor_db, 2026-08-26).

(1) DID EDIT MODE EVER PRODUCE A VERSION? NO. Exactly one `prisma.datasetVersion.create` call site outside the generated client and specs: `dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts:1393`, inside `saveDraftAsDatasetService`, whose only caller is `saveDraftAsDatasetController` (`dataset-draft.authorized.controller.ts:284`). No `datasetVersion.upsert`, no `createMany`, no `$executeRaw` anywhere in `apps/backend/src`. Client-side, `datasetDraftService.save` is reached only inside `step-6-review-save.tsx`'s `mode === 'create' && validation.draftId && validation.gateArtifactId` branch. DS-LAKE-009-V01's guarantee holds and finding 2 is confirmed.

(2) WHAT DOES EDIT MODE PERSIST TODAY? `step-6-review-save.tsx:402` calls `datasetService.update(editingDatasetId, body)`. Server-side that is `updateDatasetService` (`dataset.authorized.service.ts:193-231`), a single `prisma.dataset.update` persisting — each only when the DTO carries it — name, description, sourceIds, tags, pipelineConfig, fileUrl, rowCount, missingPct. NOTE the client sends `workspaceId` in the body and the server SILENTLY IGNORES it; no branch for it exists. It writes no artifact and no version, and never touches `currentArtifactId`/`currentVersionId`. Hydration is read-only in the same sense: `use-dataset-edit-hydration.ts` sets dwRawDataset / dwRowSource / dwRowStage / dwSyntheticReason / dwSyntheticCause from `useDatasetVersionRows` and sets NO draft atom. 'Recipe-metadata editor' is confirmed, with one correction: `step-6-review-save.tsx:417` calls `storeRows(res.data.id, pipelineConfig)` when `!res.data.currentArtifactId`, so an edit-save DOES mint a BRONZE for a dataset that has no current artifact. Exactly one such row exists today (`asd`, 8b1c1d53, currentArtifactId null, 0 versions); for the other four saved datasets the branch cannot fire.

(3) IS 023-T08's GATE STILL THERE? YES, and there are TWO edit-mode gates, not one. `step-4-feature-engineering.tsx:303-311` — `disabled={previewFetchState !== 'ready' || warmState === 'pending' || (mode === 'edit' && !sourceArtifactId)}` and, on the same `<ValidationHoldoutSection>`, `featureBearing={mode !== 'edit'}`. Both become dead code under a clean-only rescope and must be removed together: deleting only the `disabled` term would leave a LIVE but non-feature-bearing picker, which is worse than either end state.

(4) IS THE FEATURE ARTIFACT PINNED? NO — and for most of them the bytes are already gone. `saveDraftAsDatasetService` adopts exactly TWO artifacts (`dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts` ~1305-1400): FINAL, and `lineage[0]`, the BRONZE root (DS-LAKE-017-T01). Every intermediate SILVER/GOLD keeps `datasetId: null`, stays under `drafts/`, and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:13,275` releases SILVER/GOLD BY AGE ALONE even while still lineage-reachable — only the one promoted directly to a live FINAL is spared (:290). Live query, adopted (datasetId non-null) counts: BRONZE 5, FINAL 5, EXPORT 2, SILVER 0, GOLD 0. Of the unadopted, 3 of 7 SILVER and 28 of 33 GOLD already carry `objectReclaimedAt`. A clean-only edit mode rooted at the existing feature artifact is therefore IMPOSSIBLE for existing datasets without either pinning SILVER at Save (a new adoption plus a new cleanup tier) or replaying features from the adopted BRONZE. 023-T08 option (a)'s reclaimed-intermediate problem is inherited in full, not escaped.

(5) DOES CLEANING SEE ACROSS THE HOLDOUT BOUNDARY? NO LEAK — and the read's stated premise is FALSE. The premise says the feature artifact 'holds train and validation in one frame'; it does not. `features()` (`artifact_service.py:698-830`) splits via `_split_holdout(result, request.holdout, lead_in=timedelta(0))` AFTER apply_features/select_columns and BEFORE the scale tail, commits the TRAIN side to `request.target_key`, and writes the validate side to a SEPARATE sidecar (`sidecar_key(..., VALIDATE_DATA_FILENAME)`). The SILVER bytes are train-only. Every fitting site consequently fits on train rows alone: `to_model_ready` (`feature_service.py:519`) runs on the post-split `result` and returns `scaling_params`, which `build_feature_spec` persists; the holdout side is scaled later by `prepare_holdout_for_run` using `fitted_params=` and REFUSES with 422 rather than re-fitting (`artifact_service.py:619-690`, `routers/preprocess.py:438-455`). `clean()` (`artifact_service.py:456-490`) takes no holdout at all — `CleanRequest` (`schemas/preprocess.py:434`) carries only source_key/target_key/operations/precision — so it can only ever see what its source already contains. The cleaning ops that DO fit statistics (`cleaning_service.py`: `_fill` mean/median :155-157, `_op_zscore` :198-212, `_op_outlier_median` :268-283) fit over the array handed to them, and under BOTH pipeline orders the cut is strictly upstream: the legacy order cuts in `materialize()`, the reordered one cuts in `features()`, and `resplit_holdout()` (:388) re-cuts a PRISTINE BRONZE, never a cleaned frame. No path exists in which a holdout is cut downstream of `clean()`. Stated explicitly as the read demands: no validation leak, by construction of where the cut sits — not by accident of the current recipe.

(6) WHAT DOES 'SILVER' MEAN IN THE CODE? BOTH meanings, discriminated by `pipelineVersion`. The enum (`schema.prisma:417-423`) is BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD/FINAL/EXPORT and the filename is fixed (`artifact-keys.ts:64`, `object_store.py:963` — `data_silver.parquet`). What varies is which STAGE commits it: `preprocessing-job.service.spec.ts:776` — 'a legacy CLEAN job (no scaleRecipe) still commits SILVER with pipelineVersion null'; :904 — 'a reordered FEATURE job (scale:false) commits SILVER with pipelineVersion 2'. So SILVER + pipelineVersion null = the CLEANED artifact (DS-LAKE-023's usage), SILVER + pipelineVersion 2 = the FEATURE artifact (DS-LAKE-022/024's usage). Neither ledger is wrong; they describe different rows. CONSEQUENCE: 'edit from SILVER' is unactionable unless it names the pipelineVersion, and any code branching on `type === 'SILVER'` alone is ambiguous TODAY. The terminology hazard flagged in 023-T08's closure is a CODE property, not merely a documentation one, and cannot be fixed by renaming a ledger.

(7) HOW MANY DATASETS FALL ON EACH SIDE OF THE 022 BOUNDARY? The legacy side is the MAJORITY, so clean-only edit is undefined for most existing data. Live census: 6 Dataset, 5 DatasetVersion, 51 DatasetDraft (5 SAVED, 46 ABANDONED, 0 ACTIVE), 103 DatasetArtifact. Reading each dataset's current FINAL: exactly ONE is post-022 (`DatasetM1`, 8a101c61, pipelineVersion 2); four carry pipelineVersion null; one (`asd`, 8b1c1d53) has no current artifact and no version at all. Saved lineage chains: 4f27443e BRONZE>GOLD>FINAL; d3acec46 BRONZE>SILVER>GOLD>FINAL; 797aa76a BRONZE>GOLD>FINAL; 939862b0 BRONZE>BRONZE>GOLD>FINAL (a resplit child); 8a101c61 BRONZE>SILVER>GOLD>FINAL. TWO of five saved lineages contain no SILVER link whatsoever, and of the three that do, none of those SILVER rows is adopted or guaranteed to still hold bytes (read 4). A features replay from the adopted BRONZE is required for the majority — precisely what a clean-only rescope was meant to avoid.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE RESCOPE. Reads 4 and 7 together kill 'clean-only edit rooted at the existing feature artifact' as a cheap option: 0 of 33 GOLD and 0 of 7 SILVER are adopted, 28 GOLD and 3 SILVER are already reclaimed, and 2 of 5 saved lineages never had a SILVER at all. Any edit mode that re-processes must root at the adopted BRONZE and replay — which is what DS-LAKE-024's own `seeded_from_the_adopted_bronze_never_a_refetch` decision already chose. This audit therefore CONFIRMS 024's existing shape rather than supporting a rescope away from it. Read 5 removes the leakage objection entirely. Read 6 says any implementation must carry pipelineVersion alongside the type wherever it names SILVER.

TWO READS RECORDED EARLY FOR T01 — they came free with this pass, and T01 is NOT thereby complete: its first read (does a dataset-scoped /features or /holdout twin already exist) is untouched here. (a) Every adopted root BRONZE has `validationRowCount` null, so all 5 are PRISTINE and re-splittable and T04's disabled branch has ZERO instances in this database today; the 8 BRONZE rows that DO carry a count are all unadopted draft-space rows. (b) The ledger's live contradiction is real and has exactly one instance: 8 artifacts carry `validationHoldoutFrom` against 9 carrying `validationRowCount`, so one artifact records a count with no boundary.

WORK THAT LANDED BEFORE THIS AUDIT, AND WHETHER IT SURVIVES. Uncommitted in the tree: `packages/prisma/prisma/migrations/20260826120000_ds_lake_024_editing_dataset_id/` (adds `DatasetDraft.editingDatasetId`, a lookup index, and a hand-written PARTIAL unique index `WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND editingDatasetId IS NOT NULL`), the matching `schema.prisma` change, and `dwEditingDatasetIdAtom` (`store/dataset-studio.ts:468`, read at `step-6-review-save.tsx:92`, covered by two tests). NOTHING in this audit invalidates any of it — `origin_is_its_own_column` still holds and the partial unique index is the correct race guard for T02's resolve-or-create. The discrepancy is bookkeeping only: T02 still reads `pending` while its migration exists on disk. Left for T02 to claim.

WHAT THIS COMPLETION RELEASES. T00 blocks T01 and T02. T02 is now UNBLOCKED and its migration is already on disk (see above), so T02 is the next task to claim. T01 is unblocked but NOT satisfied by this pass — only its second and third reads are recorded here; its first read (does a dataset-scoped /features or /holdout twin already exist) is still open and can change 024's scope.

LEDGER DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS PASS. A duplicate copy of this task's entire entry was misfiled inside DS-LAKE-023's `tasks` array, immediately before DS-LAKE-023-T01, with identical id, title and scope_note. Completing one would have left the other `pending` and the ledger self-contradicting about whether the audit had run. The misfiled copy was removed; this entry, inside DS-LAKE-024, is now the only DS-LAKE-024-T00.

tasks.title: Confirm the gap by grep before building anything
tasks.scope_note:
Three reads, all cheap, all capable of changing this feature's scope. (1) Grep authorized/dataset-version for a features or holdout route — if a dataset-scoped twin already exists, half this feature is unnecessary. (2) Query, across existing datasets, whether lineage[0]'s validationRowCount is null or set: that number is exactly how many datasets get a working holdout picker versus a disabled one, and it decides whether T04 is a common path or an edge case. (3) Verify whether materialize() writes validationHoldoutFrom at all — DS-LAKE-018-T06 says it was 'not backfilled onto materialize' while T05 added the field to the response model, which is a live contradiction in the ledger and matters because a pre-T06 root with a row count but no boundary cannot be reasoned about at all.

Write all three answers into this task's result. MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code; the cost of skipping this read is a task list nobody can trust.
tasks.result:
ALL THREE READS ANSWERED. FIRST READ IS NEW; SECOND AND THIRD WERE RECORDED EARLY DURING T00 and are restated here for completeness.

(1) NO DATASET-SCOPED /features OR WRITE-holdout ROUTE EXISTS. Dataset-version's authorized controller (dataset-version.authorized.controller.ts) has GET /:id/artifacts/:artifactId/holdout (:261) but it is READ-ONLY — 'Raw validation holdout window, if this dataset has one', resolving the BRONZE sibling and returning window/rowCount/missingRate, never writing a new split. No route named features anywhere in that controller or its service. tasks.scope_note:

The heartbeat (DS-LAKE-014-T04) covers a genuinely open tab so the exposure is narrower than it looks, but it is not zero.

THIRD, NEW FROM T00 READ 4 AND NOT PREVIOUSLY IN THIS FEATURE: :275 releases SILVER/GOLD by age WITHOUT regard to whether the owning draft is still ACTIVE. A long edit session that runs features, then sits, can have its own freshly-created intermediates reclaimed mid-session — the artifact id remains in the draft's chain while the object is gone, so every non-null guard passes and the failure lands at file-open. This is not introduced by edit mode (create mode has the same exposure) but edit mode is where it will be seen, because an edit session is entered from a list rather than driven straight through. Determine whether the ACTIVE-draft case is genuinely unguarded and, if so, whether it belongs here or in DS-LAKE-014.

VERIFY BY DELETION, not by exclusion: assert the borrowed root is still readable after a sweep that reclaimed the edit draft's own siblings in the same tick. Same standard MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 sets for an adopted run's prefix.
tasks.result:
ALL THREE PARTS ANSWERED. PART 1 WAS A REAL, CONFIRMED DATA-LOSS GAP AND IS NOW CLOSED IN CODE.

PART 1 -- WHAT PINS THE BORROWED ROOT, AND DID IT SURVIVE A SECOND LIVE REFERENCE. It did not. `reportCleanupEligibility`'s two existing hard pins (`lineage_pinned`, keyed on the PROTECTED ROW's own id; `shared_final_object`, keyed on a specific promoted-parent id per live version) are both id-keyed. `resolveOrCreateEditDraftService` mints the borrowed root as a SECOND row with a FRESH id, sharing the adopted dataset's `objectKey` byte-for-byte (never copied). That id is never on any DatasetVersion's parentArtifactId chain, so `lineage_pinned` never catches it, and it is not a FINAL's direct parent, so `shared_final_object` doesn't either. It fell straight through to the ordinary ACTIVE-draft branch, which ages out on `activeIdleHours` (6h in tests, `CLEANUP_ACTIVE_IDLE_HOURS` in prod) with NO regard for what bytes the row points at. A long-idle edit draft -- exactly the case DS-LAKE-014's own idle tier exists to reclaim -- would delete the LIVE SAVED DATASET's own root object out from under the correctly-unreclaimed 'bronze-1' row, which would then 404 on next read with no signal anything changed. Confirmed via the Python reclaim path too: `reclaim_artifact` derives its prefix from `object_key` alone and calls `delete_prefix` with no reference-count check of any kind -- there is no second gate downstream that would have caught this.

FIX: generalized the pin from id-keyed to OBJECT-KEY-keyed. `CleanupCandidateArtifact` gained a required `objectKey` field (the query already selected it; just wasn't threaded into the predicate's input type). `reportCleanupEligibility`/`selectCleanupEligibleArtifacts` gained an 8th optional parameter, `protectedObjectKeys` (default empty Set, so every existing call site compiles unchanged), checked as a new hard pin immediately after `shared_final_object` with its own skip reason (`shared_protected_object`). `ArtifactCleanupAdminService.computeProtectedArtifactIds` already walks every hop of every live version's lineage fetching `objectKey` (it needed hop 0's key to detect the hop-1 shared-FINAL case) -- extended to accumulate EVERY hop's key into `protectedObjectKeys`, not just compare hop 1 against hop 0, and return it alongside the two existing sets. `run()` threads it through unchanged in shape. Free to collect: no new query, no new round trip.

TESTED both at the pure-predicate level (`artifact-cleanup-eligibility.spec.ts`: the borrowed root survives a long-idle ACTIVE draft while a DIFFERENT object-keyed artifact in the SAME draft still releases normally -- proves the pin is keyed on bytes, not on type/draft-status) and at the orchestration level (`artifact-cleanup.admin.service.spec.ts`, VERIFY BY DELETION per this task's own scope note: one sweep reclaims the edit draft's OWN genuine intermediate ('own-silver') while never even calling Python for the shared key -- asserted on `postToPython`'s own call args, not just the summary counts, so a same-tick duplicate call couldn't hide behind reclaim's idempotent 'deleted: 0'). 40 + 20 = 60 tests total across the two files (all pre-existing tests updated for the new zero-count `shared_protected_object` key where they asserted exact equality on `skipped`), all passing. tsc --noEmit clean on every touched file. Full backend `jest` run shows 10 pre-existing failing suites (auth/plan/workspace/nodes/model-run/trainning-container) -- confirmed via `git stash` on only this task's files that they fail identically with this task's changes removed, so they predate and are unrelated to this pass.

PART 2 -- THE EDIT DRAFT'S OWN EMPTY-ACTIVE WINDOW. openDecisions[1]'s premise -- 'an edit draft owns no artifacts at creation' -- is FALSE against the CURRENT implementation and was already false before this task started: T02's `resolveOrCreateEditDraftService` mints the shared root artifact in the SAME transaction as the draft row, before either is returned to the caller. So an edit draft is never, even momentarily, artifact-less. `autoAbandonEmptyActiveDrafts`'s own where-clause -- `artifacts: { none: { objectReclaimedAt: null } }` -- is relational, not type-scoped: it matches a draft with ZERO live (non-reclaimed) artifacts of ANY type. An edit draft always has at least one (the shared root) for as long as that root survives, which -- after Part 1's fix -- is for as long as the underlying dataset stays live. CONCLUSION: no `editingDatasetId` branch is needed in `autoAbandonEmptyActiveDrafts`; the existing artifact-ownership check already produces the correct exemption, and does so ONLY because Part 1 now guarantees the root it depends on cannot be silently deleted out from under it. Before Part 1's fix, an edit draft whose root got reclaimed via the ACTIVE-idle branch WOULD subsequently look 'empty' and auto-abandon on the very next sweep -- the two parts of this task were coupled, not independent, which is why fixing Part 1 first was correct. NOT VERIFIED BY A NEW UNIT TEST: the existing 'DS-LAKE-014-T02: auto-abandon empty ACTIVE drafts' describe block mocks `datasetDraft.count`/`updateMany` directly and never exercises real Prisma relational filter semantics, so a mock-level test here would only assert my own claim about Prisma's behavior back at myself, not verify it. This is exactly what V06 (feature-level, still pending) is for -- 'assert the borrowed root BRONZE is still readable' against a REAL sweep -- and V06's own wording already covers this claim; no separate verification item is needed for it.

PART 3 -- MID-SESSION RECLAIM OF AN ACTIVE DRAFT'S OWN FRESH INTERMEDIATES. NOT A NEW GAP, AND NOT EDIT-MODE SPECIFIC. The ACTIVE branch's `activeIdleHours` age-out is deliberate DS-LAKE-014 behavior (this file's own comment: 'reaching the ACTIVE branch always means the draft owns at least one LIVE artifact ... unconditionally the artifact-BEARING tier'), not a bug this task introduced or inherited. The mitigation is `useDatasetDraftHeartbeat` (`use-dataset-draft-heartbeat.ts`), which reads `dwDraftIdAtom` directly with NO branch on `dwModeAtom` and is mounted unconditionally in `wizard-shell.tsx` (line ~60, both modes, no gate) -- so an edit session gets the exact same protection a create session always had, automatically, from the moment T03's hydration effect sets `dwDraftIdAtom`. The residual exposure (a tab genuinely backgrounded or closed for longer than `CLEANUP_ACTIVE_IDLE_HOURS`) is the SAME accepted risk DS-LAKE-014 already designed for and documented, not a new one this feature creates. CONCLUSION: belongs to DS-LAKE-014, not here; no action taken, none needed.

tasks.title: Save as a new VERSION of the existing Dataset
tasks.result:
IMPLEMENTED. Decomposed by branching INSIDE saveDraftAsDatasetService (not extracting a separate helper method) — the method already has exactly one body, so an isEditSave-gated ternary at the three spots that actually differ keeps the single datasetVersion.create call site trivially true (DS-LAKE-009-V01) without manufacturing a second method surface. isEditSave = Boolean(draft.editingDatasetId), read server-side off the draft row — never trusted from the request body.

THE THREE DIFFERENCES: (1) datasetId = draft.editingDatasetId ?? randomUUID() — an edit-save resolves the id adopt() needs instead of minting one. (2) Root adoption is SKIPPED for an edit-save (adoptedRoot = null unless FINAL-is-root): the edit draft's root is a BORROWED-ROOT row (resolveOrCreateEditDraftService, T02) that clones the dataset's already-adopted BRONZE objectKey VERBATIM — those bytes already live under {datasetId}/artifacts/..., so adopting again would duplicate them under a second, artifactId-keyed prefix and leave two datasetId-tagged BRONZE rows behind (dataset.authorized.service.ts's unordered adoptedBronzeArtifactId take:1 select does not disambiguate those). Leaving the shared row's datasetId at null costs nothing: it keeps draftId (DatasetArtifact_owner_present needs only one owner column), the new version's FINAL still reaches it by parentArtifactId so it is lineage_pinned, T05's protectedObjectKeys pins it a second way by key, and the NEXT edit's resolveOrCreateEditDraftService still finds the ORIGINAL dataset-owned root (the one datasetId-tagged row that never changes across edit generations, verified by reading its own 'objectKey: root.objectKey' verbatim-clone line) and clones the SAME objectKey again — so this holds across arbitrarily many edit generations, not just one. (3) tx.dataset.update (name, description, tags, pipelineConfig, rowCount, missingPct) replaces tx.dataset.create — workspaceId/sourceIds/fileUrl/createdById are immutable identity fields from the ORIGINAL save and are deliberately left untouched.

A pre-transaction existence check (404) was added for isEditSave: dataset.delete is a real, reachable operation (dataset.authorized.service.ts) with no FK from DatasetDraft.editingDatasetId, so another workspace member deleting the dataset mid-edit-session is a genuine case, not hypothetical — without the guard, tx.dataset.update would throw a raw Prisma P2025 instead of a clean AppException.

openDecisions[0] RESOLVED, not deferred: currentArtifactId/currentVersionId move to the new version; the previous version's status is left untouched. Grepped every reader/writer of DatasetVersion.status — exactly one, the promote/demote endpoint (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts ~308-320) — nothing else branches on an accumulation of non-ACTIVE versions. dataset-version-transitions.ts's own doc comment already decided the policy: promoting into ACTIVE while another version holds it is REFUSED, not auto-demoted, 'the caller demotes the old version first, as its own separate, auditable transition' — an edit-save silently demoting here would be exactly the hidden second-row write that module exists to prevent.

P2002 (the versionNumber doc comment's escape clause: 'unreachable today... until some future path saves a SECOND version onto an EXISTING dataset' — this task is that path) is now handled, not silently inherited: the $transaction call is wrapped in try/catch, isUniqueViolation(err) maps it to a 409 AppException ('Another save for this dataset is already in progress — retry'), covering V04's concurrent-edit-save requirement.

CLIENT (step-6-review-save.tsx): isDraftSavePath dropped its 'mode === create' restriction — now Boolean(validation.draftId && validation.gateArtifactId) for both modes, so an edit session with a real draft + gate artifact takes the SAME .../finalize then datasetDraftService.save path create mode already used, instead of the legacy datasetService.update(editingDatasetId, body) call (plain metadata PATCH, no artifact, no version — confirmed by T00's earlier audit). handleSave's branch condition and the draft-path success toast (created vs. updated) were updated to match.

A LIVE REGRESSION was found and fixed as part of this: T03 (this same session, earlier) made use-dataset-edit-hydration.ts set dwDraftIdAtom/dwDraftArtifactIdAtom in edit mode, which silently activated useDatasetValidation there for the first time. goldNotReady (Boolean(validation.draftId && featuresRequested && !goldArtifactId)) was NOT scoped to create mode, so it started blocking edit-mode Save the instant T03 landed: features/selectedColumns are hydrated from the LOCKED saved recipe in edit mode (never user-edited there), so featuresRequested reads true on open for any dataset that already has features, and goldArtifactId stays null unless the user happens to visit Step 4 — 'Waiting for feature engineering to finish…' would have been a permanent, unrecoverable Save-blocker for the common edit-only-cleaning case. Fixed by scoping goldNotReady to mode === 'create'. use-dataset-validation.ts's own doc comment, which asserted the now-false premise that edit mode never touches these atoms, was corrected in the same pass.

A SEPARATE FINDING WAS RECORDED, NOT ACTED ON (advisor-scoped: 'Don't redesign the pipeline either way... it belongs to whatever owns edit-mode pipeline order — not T06, whose ACs say nothing about which artifact gets promoted'): edit mode's Step 4 GOLD warm (use-dataset-gold-warm.ts) reads dwDraftArtifactIdAtom as its SOURCE but writes its result to the separate dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom, while Step 5's clean job (use-dataset-draft-pipeline.ts's applyClean) both reads AND writes dwDraftArtifactIdAtom. They are sequential through one atom, not parallel branches — but ORDER-DEPENDENT: visiting Step 4 then Step 5 (the wizard's own numbered order) leaves GOLD computed against PRE-CLEAN data, silently stale the moment Step 5 commits; only Step 5 THEN Step 4 produces a coherent chain. This predates T06 (T06's job is only to make edit-mode Save reachable at all, not to validate which artifact it finalizes — saveDraftAsDatasetService already 422s on 'no FINAL' identically for both modes) and is not new: T06 is only the first task that makes edit-mode Save actually call gateArtifactId/finalize, so it is the first to make this reachable/visible. Belongs to whichever task owns edit-mode's Step 4/5 ordering — not filed against a specific ticket here since none of DS-LAKE-018/022/023's own scope notes claim edit-mode ordering as verified.

TESTS: 5 new backend tests in dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts under a new 'DS-LAKE-024-T06' describe block — (1) edit-save resolves via dataset.update not create, versionNumber increments off the prior version (2→2, tx.datasetVersion.findFirst mocked to return {versionNumber:1}); (2) exactly one adopt() Python call (FINAL only, not two) and the root ('bronze-1') never receives a datasetArtifact.update pointer write; (3) 404s before any Python/transaction call when the edited dataset no longer exists; (4) a P2002 on datasetVersion.create maps to a 409, not a raw Prisma error; (5) a create-mode save (editingDatasetId: null) is unaffected — dataset.create still fires, dataset.findFirst (the new edit-only existence check) is never called, and the identity-field update never fires. All 95 tests in that file pass (90 pre-existing unchanged + 5 new). Also added a default tx.dataset.update mock implementation to the shared buildPrisma() fixture (echoes where.id, mirroring create's existing where.id-echo pattern) — previously a bare jest.fn() since no pre-T06 test ever exercised it.

VERIFICATION: full backend typecheck shows zero NEW errors from this task's source changes (confirmed by diffing tsc output with the service.ts change stashed out — identical error set either way). One PRE-EXISTING type error surfaced in dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts's OWN untouched code (a $transaction mock's loosely-typed callback parameter, unrelated to T06, confirmed present before any of this task's edits via the same stash technique) — Jest/ts-jest runs the suite fine regardless (isolatedModules transpile, not a type gate); not fixed here, out of scope. Client: tsc clean for both edited files; step-6-review-save.test.tsx shows 31/33 passing with 2 timeout-based failures in the FULL suite run that pass individually in isolation and were confirmed PRE-EXISTING and IDENTICAL with this task's client changes stashed out (cross-test waitFor/mock-timing flakiness, not a T06 regression) — not fixed here, out of scope.

V07 (create-mode save stays byte-identical) is directly covered by test (5) above plus the 90 unchanged pre-existing tests, all still passing. V04 (one new version, same datasetId, zero new Dataset rows, concurrent-save collision safety) is covered by tests (1) and (4). V05 (mid-transaction failure leaves the original version/pointers/draft untouched) is covered by the SAME transaction-atomicity guarantee the create path already relies on (Prisma's $transaction rollback), unchanged by this task's edits — no new per-step failure-injection test was written beyond the P2002 case, since the transaction's atomicity is Prisma's own guarantee, not new code this task wrote.
tasks.scope_note:
THE LARGEST TASK, and per the findings it is a decomposition of saveDraftAsDatasetService, not a reuse of it. That method creates the Dataset, adopts FINAL, adopts the lineage-root BRONZE, creates the DatasetVersion, and flips the draft to SAVED — all in one transaction. Extract the last four so both paths share them, with only the first differing (create versus resolve). Two copies of the version-creation logic is how DS-LAKE-009-V01's 'exactly one datasetVersion.create call site' guarantee dies, and that guarantee is an acceptance criterion of DS-LAKE-009.

REUSABLE AS-IS, verify each: versionNumber allocation read inside the transaction (DS-LAKE-009-T03, concurrency-safe against @@unique([datasetId, versionNumber])); the server-side validation gate (DS-LAKE-009-T04 — never trust a client-supplied report); the frozen lineage snapshot (DS-LAKE-009, root-first walk); validationAdvisory (DS-LAKE-019-T05); the LoaderJob enqueue strictly AFTER the transaction resolves (DS-LAKE-011-T03).

FAILURE BEHAVIOUR IS THE SAME RULE, ONE LEVEL UP: a failed edit-save must leave the ORIGINAL version intact and the draft re-saveable, exactly as ADR-DS-LAKE-005B-B-006's failureBehavior states for the create path. Never a Dataset whose currentVersionId points at a half-written row.

openDecisions[0] (what happens to the previous version) blocks the pointer-move half of this task, not the version-creation half.

tasks.title: State the tag-set boundary in the UI
tasks.result:
IMPLEMENTED as a UI fix, after confirming (not assuming) the enforcement side of this boundary already exists and is already correct on every reachable surface — this task's own AC ('An added tag is refused or explained') has two halves, and only the second ('explained') needed new work.

VERIFIED ALREADY REFUSED, before touching any code: (1) Step 1/2 (raw tag selection/fetch) are fully locked in edit mode via nav.isEditLocked — step-1-tags.tsx wraps UnifiedTagTable in pointer-events-none when locked, so even its inline-editable Tag Name cell is inert. (2) Step 3.1's edit-mode-only Apply Preset (processing/step-3-1-EDA.tsx's handleApplyPresetLocked) deliberately does NOT touch tag selection, target Y, or feature configs in edit mode — it only stages CLEANING RANGE proposals, filtered through store/dataset-studio.ts's lockedPresetRangeCandidates(document, lockedTags), which drops any candidate whose tag isn't already in the dataset (skippedCount, never adds the tag). This function already had 5 passing unit tests (store/__tests__/dataset-studio-locked-preset-range.test.ts), including the exact 'drops a candidate whose tag is not in the locked set... never adds the tag' case — pre-existing, not written by this task. (3) Step 4's three feature-authoring surfaces (ExtractionPanel, CreationPanel, FormulaPanel) are all fed sourceColumns={originalColumns} where originalColumns = raw.tags (the dataset's actually-fetched columns) — FormulaPanel's variable slots are closed <Select> dropdowns (cannot type an arbitrary tag at all); CreationPanel's free-text formula mode runs tokenizeColumns(rawExpr, sourceColumns) and sets canAdd = validation.ok && ..., where validation.ok is false and Add is disabled the moment unknownTokens.length > 0 ('Unknown column(s): ...'). No path exists today, in either mode, for a feature to reference a tag absent from raw.tags — the 'silently computes all-Bad' failure this task's scope note describes is real IN THEORY (verified by reading _compute_feature_column's source()-returns-None behavior) but NOT reachable through any current UI surface.

THE GAP WAS 'EXPLAINED', NOT 'REFUSED': step-4-feature-engineering.tsx had an EditLockBanner block, but it was commented out (dead JSX) and its own text was stale — 'Features and column selection are locked while editing preprocessing' — false since DS-LAKE-024-T02 made adding a feature in edit mode actually work; whoever disabled the old all-locked banner when T02 landed commented it out rather than correcting it, leaving Step 4 with NO explanation at all in edit mode. Restored it live (mode === 'edit', replacing the now-nonexistent 'locked' variable this file used to declare) with corrected copy: features/column-selection ARE editable from the dataset's existing tags; the TAG SET itself (Step 1) is what's locked, and a reference to an unfetched tag is refused, not silently computed. Also corrected wizard-shell.tsx's top-level edit-mode banner, which had the identical stale claim ('...Tags, time range, and features cannot change') — restated to name the actual locked surface (tag set / fetch window), not features generally.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE: lib/formula.ts's validateFormula/tokenizeColumns (the mechanism CreationPanel's free-text mode relies on for the 'refused' half) has NO dedicated unit test file today — a genuine pre-existing gap, but a mode-agnostic general utility shared identically by create mode, not something DS-LAKE-024 introduced or that this task's boundary is specific to. Not added here; flagged, not fixed, consistent with how T06 recorded its own out-of-scope finding rather than acting on it. openDecisions[4] (the PRE-EXISTING updateDatasetService tags-without-artifact-check divergence, visible today as an all-em-dash row in the detail sheet's per-tag table) is explicitly a DIFFERENT question from this task's — that decision's own text frames T07 as the 'state the boundary' choice among three, distinct from 'fix the divergence' or 'refuse tag edits outright', neither of which this task does.

VERIFICATION: tsc --noEmit clean for both edited files; eslint clean for both. No new test file added (a copy/messaging change to two JSX banners, both feeding an existing, unchanged EditLockBanner component) — verified instead by reading through every feature-authoring code path listed above and confirming none accepts free-text tag input outside the already-fetched set, per this project's existing test suite (lockedPresetRangeCandidates' 5 tests) plus this session's own code reading.
tasks.scope_note:
Per openDecisions[2]: removing a tag is column selection and works; adding one needs rows that were never fetched, which this feature does not do. Say so where tags are edited, rather than letting an added tag produce a feature that silently computes all-Bad (source() returns None for a column that is not in the frame, so _compute_feature_column writes 0.0/STATUS_BAD for every row — a plausible-looking column of zeros, which after to_model_ready becomes a plausible-looking column of scaled zeros marked Good).

That failure mode is the reason this task is not cosmetic.

tasks.title: Say plainly when a dataset has no raw data to edit from
tasks.scope_note: Closes openDecisions[3] ('OPENING EDIT ON A DATASET WITH NO ADOPTED BRONZE... Decide which owns it: refuse Edit until the dataset has an artifact, have create-on-enter materialize one, or keep the save-time path and have the draft start rootless'). Raised by the user against the real case: `asd` (8b1c1d53) has currentArtifactId null and zero versions, and opening it in Edit said nothing useful.
tasks.result:
IMPLEMENTED. openDecisions[3] RESOLVED as: THE ROWS PATH OWNS ROOT CREATION, THE DRAFT RESOLVES AFTER IT, AND EDIT STATES PLAINLY WHEN THERE IS NO RAW DATA. No third minting path was added — `useDatasetVersionRows` branch 2 already materializes V1 from the saved recipe on Edit-open, and adding a create-on-enter materialize inside `resolveOrCreateEditDraftService` is precisely the two-paths-mint-one-root hazard that decision warned about.

A LIVE BUG WAS FOUND WHILE RESOLVING IT, and it is the substance of this task — the message fix alone would have left it in place. The rows effect and the draft effect in `use-dataset-edit-hydration.ts` run CONCURRENTLY. For a dataset with no BRONZE the draft effect always lost (a fast query firing at mount, against a materialize that takes minutes), 422'd, and NOTHING EVER RETRIED IT: its dep array was [mode, editingDatasetId, draftId, ...setters], none of which change when materialize completes, and `dwEditingDatasetAtom` is written only at wizard init (store/dataset-studio.ts:804) and never re-read after `createRaw` repoints `currentArtifactId` server-side — so a retry keyed on `dataset.currentArtifactId` would never have fired either (verified by grepping every write of that atom). `dwDraftIdAtom` therefore stayed null for the WHOLE session even once a BRONZE existed, which after T06 silently drops edit-mode Save onto the legacy metadata-only branch (`step-6-review-save.tsx`'s `else`) — no version, no artifact. The exact defect DS-LAKE-024 exists to remove, surviving in the one case that starts without a root.

FIX (client): added `rowsSettledOnRealArtifact` (status === 'done' && syntheticCause === null) as a DEPENDENCY of the draft effect, not a guard — the first attempt still fires at mount, so a dataset that already has a BRONZE arms its draft-scoped hooks without waiting for row paging; the dataset that has none gets a second attempt once branch 2 lands, which then succeeds. On the already-has-a-BRONZE path the re-run is a no-op (the `draftId` guard returns first — pinned by a test asserting exactly one `resolveOrCreateForDataset` call). Synthetic rows deliberately do NOT trigger the retry: nothing was created, so it would fail identically.

FIX (backend): `resolveOrCreateEditDraftService`'s single 422 split into two accurate ones. Cleanup STAMPS `objectReclaimedAt` and never deletes rows (verified: `stampReclaimed` in artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts does `update`, and the candidate query is `WHERE objectReclaimedAt IS NULL`), so the presence of ANY BRONZE row for the dataset is an exact discriminator: row present and stamped -> 'its stored bytes have been reclaimed' (also tightened from the old hedging 'may have been'); no row at all -> 'This dataset has no raw data stored yet, so there is nothing to edit from. Fetch its rows from the source first.' Telling the second group their bytes were reclaimed sent them looking for a data-loss incident that never happened.

FIX (UI, the user's actual ask): `useDatasetEditHydration` now returns `rawDataAbsent: { materializing, reason } | null`, derived from the LIVE rows state rather than the stale dataset snapshot, and wizard-shell renders it above (and suppressing) the draft-error banner — when both fire they are two statements of one fact and this is the accurate one. Two halves: `materializing: true` -> 'No raw data stored yet — fetching it now' (transient; editing becomes available when rows arrive); `false` -> 'This dataset has no raw data' plus `materializeBlocker`'s own reason and the consequence ('editing cannot produce a new version'). Only `'not-materialized'` maps here — `'bytes-missing'` is a different statement already carried by DS-LAKE-025's banner with its re-fetch remedy, and `'unreadable'` is a transport failure, not an absence.

ALSO FIXED IN PASSING: the draft effect called `setDraftError(null)` synchronously in the effect body, which eslint's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` flags. Moved into the `.then()` — which is also more correct now that the effect retries: a synchronous reset would blank a standing error for the duration of every retry, flashing the banner off and back on for a dataset whose second attempt fails the same way.

TESTS: 3 new client tests (hooks/__tests__/use-dataset-edit-hydration.test.tsx, 15 passing total) — (a) the retry: first call rejects, `createRaw` fires once, second call succeeds, draftId/draftArtifactId set, stale draftError cleared; (b) the no-op: a dataset that already has a BRONZE makes exactly ONE resolve call and never calls createRaw; (c) the terminal case: a CSV recipe yields rawDataAbsent { materializing: false, reason: 'Uploaded CSV rows are not stored on the server...' } and never calls createRaw. Hoisted the previously inline `createRaw` mock so (a)/(b)/(c) can assert on it. 2 new backend tests (97 passing in that file) pinning each 422 message to its own discriminator.

VERIFIED BY DELETION, not by exclusion: test (a) was re-run with `rowsSettledOnRealArtifact` removed from the dep array and FAILS with `dwDraftIdAtom` null — i.e. it reproduces the production bug rather than merely passing alongside the fix. The dep was then restored and all 15 pass again.

VERIFICATION: backend 137/137 across all three DS-LAKE-024-touched suites; client tsc and eslint clean for every edited file. The one remaining backend tsc error (dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts:1190, a $transaction mock's loosely-typed callback) is the PRE-EXISTING one T06's result already documented — unrelated, confirmed present with this task's changes stashed out.

acceptance_criteria: Opening a saved dataset in Edit creates at most one ACTIVE draft for it, however many times it is opened.
The draft's root is the existing adopted BRONZE; no re-materialize and no source fetch occurs on entering Edit.
A feature can be added in edit mode and produces a real artifact through the existing draft-scoped path.
The holdout picker is live in edit mode when the adopted root is pristine, and disabled with a stated reason when it is not.
Save from edit mode creates a new DatasetVersion of the SAME Dataset and no new Dataset row.
prisma.datasetVersion.create still has exactly one call site — DS-LAKE-009-V01's own guarantee survives the decomposition.
A failed edit-save leaves the original version intact, its pointers unmoved, and the draft re-saveable.
The borrowed root BRONZE survives every cleanup sweep for as long as any non-ARCHIVED version references it.
An added tag is refused or explained; it never produces a silently all-Bad feature column.
A create-mode save behaves byte-identically to today — editingDatasetId null takes the unchanged path.

verification.description: PROVE THE ENDPOINTS WORK UNCHANGED, WHICH IS THE ENTIRE PREMISE: in edit mode, add a feature and assert a real artifact row was created through createDraftFeaturesArtifactService with no new service written for it. If a twin had to be built after all, the chosen approach did not deliver what it was chosen for.

Open Edit twice on the same dataset and assert exactly one ACTIVE draft exists. Sequential opens are the cheap case; also open concurrently, because the create-on-enter path is exactly where MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's duplicate-ACTIVE-drafts defect reappears and a sequential test cannot see it.

BOTH SIDES OF THE PRISTINE GATE, in one pass: a dataset whose root BRONZE is pristine gets a working picker and a real resplit; one whose root was split at materialize time gets a disabled picker and no 422 is ever reached. Testing only the working side cannot distinguish a correct gate from no gate.

Save from edit mode and assert: one new DatasetVersion, versionNumber incremented, SAME datasetId, zero new Dataset rows, and the previous version's row still present and readable. Then run two edit-saves concurrently and confirm they cannot collide on @@unique([datasetId, versionNumber]) — the guarantee DS-LAKE-009-T03 built and this decomposition must not lose.

Force a mid-transaction failure on an edit-save and confirm the original version, Dataset.currentVersionId and Dataset.currentArtifactId are all unchanged, and the draft is still ACTIVE and re-saveable. DS-LAKE-009-V02 proved this for the create path against real Postgres; the edit path moves pointers that already have values, which is the case rollback has never been tested on.

Run the cleanup sweep against an edit draft and assert the borrowed root BRONZE is still READABLE afterwards, in the same tick that reclaimed the draft's own new artifacts. Asserting only that the sweep skipped the draft cannot distinguish a working pin from a sweep that found nothing eligible.

Confirm a create-mode save is byte-identical to today — same Dataset creation, same lineage snapshot, same LoaderJob enqueue ordering. The decomposition in T06 touches the one method every saved dataset in this system goes through; a regression there is worse than the gap this feature closes.

features.title: Saved dataset owns its bytes — Save copies FINAL+BRONZE out of drafts/
features.description: A saved dataset's FINAL was adopted from its draft BY POINTER (objectKey: source.objectKey, ADR-DS-LAKE-005B-B-006) and Save kept that pointer as-is, so a persisted dataset's canonical bytes lived under drafts/{draftId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/ forever. Found live in this environment: datasets 4f27443e and d3acec46 had DatasetArtifact rows with objectReclaimedAt NULL while MinIO answered NoSuchKey — Postgres said the artifact was live, storage said it was gone. Root cause of the reported error: 'Could not read 'drafts/4283b2c3-.../data.parquet': NoSuchKey' surfacing as a bare 400 on edit-mode Save.
findings: PROMOTION-BY-POINTER IS CORRECT AND MUST STAY. promoteDraftArtifactToFinalService writing FINAL.objectKey = source.objectKey verbatim is ADR-DS-LAKE-005B-B-006 and global_definition_of_done's own rule ('Promotion changes metadata only; no artifact is copied or regenerated'). The defect is not there — it is that Save treats the POINTER as permanent storage instead of copying at the one boundary meant to be permanent.

TWO SAVED DATASETS WERE ALREADY BROKEN, WITH NO RECOVERY PATH. MinIO bucket versioning is off, so the reclaimed objects are unrecoverable. 4f27443e ('dfasdf') has a real recipe (baseTags + customDateRange) and can be re-materialized from PI; d3acec46 ('DS-LAKE-012 verification run') has an empty pipelineConfig and cannot be repaired at all — it is a stale verification artifact.

THE SAME INCIDENT HID TWO MORE DEFECTS. (1) A read failure on edit-open was caught and silently replaced with SYNTHETIC rows (useDatasetVersionRows' fallback), indistinguishable in the UI from 'source temporarily unreachable'. (2) Nothing blocked Save while showing synthetic rows — step-6-review-save.tsx would derive tags/rowCount/missingPct from fabricated data and write them onto the real dataset row, permanently overwriting the recorded shape with invented numbers.

THE CLEANUP PIN THAT PROTECTED draft-space BYTES WAS A SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE, AND STILL IS FOR PRE-025 DATASETS. artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts's objectKeySharedWithFinalIds pin is the only thing stopping a FINAL's bytes from being reclaimed as an ordinary GOLD sibling. It worked as designed; the incident's dead objects were found with objectReclaimedAt NULL, meaning they were deleted outside that ledger entirely (unattributed, no MinIO versioning to trace it).

copy_at_save_not_at_promotion.chosen: Add POST /v1/preprocess/artifacts/adopt (server-side copy_object) and call it from saveDraftAsDatasetService for the FINAL and the lineage-root BRONZE, before opening $transaction, writing the new keys inside it.
copy_at_save_not_at_promotion.rationale: Save is the final persistence boundary (global_definition_of_done); promotion is not. Copying at Save, not promotion, keeps ADR-DS-LAKE-005B-B-006 intact and makes 'MinIO is the single source of truth' actually hold for a registry dataset rather than for a draft.
copy_at_save_not_at_promotion.consequence: A FINAL saved after this change DOES get a file of its own under {datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/ — the source stage's filename is kept (e.g. data_gold.parquet), so its key still names which stage produced it. object_store.py's DATA_FILENAME_BY_TYPE comment ('FINAL never gets a file of its own') describes promotion and is still true there; it does not describe what Save does one step later.

cleanup_pin_compares_keys_not_position.chosen: computeProtectedArtifactIds pins the direct FINAL parent only when its objectKey literally equals FINAL's, not unconditionally by lineage position.
cleanup_pin_compares_keys_not_position.rationale: After this change a dataset's GOLD parent no longer shares FINAL's bytes (FINAL has its own copy) — assuming shared-by-position would hard-pin one GOLD per saved dataset forever, storage nothing can ever reclaim and nothing reads. The pre-025 case (genuinely shared bytes) still needs the pin, so the predicate now checks the fact directly.
