tasks.title: Establish whether a saved dataset's values are engineering units or model-ready, and where the user was told
tasks.result:
VERDICT: not a scaling defect. FINAL is a MODEL-READY artifact by construction, and the unit change is UNDISCLOSED on every surface that reads it. The premise under test held.

(1) DEFAULTED, TWICE OVER — the user was never offered the choice. ScaleRequest.scale is Field(default=True) (schemas/preprocess.py:547). Only the CREATE-mode feature warm sends scale:false (use-dataset-gold-warm.ts:199, gated on isReordered); Step 5's clean+scale commit then runs scale() separately and unconditionally. scale()'s own docstring: 'an empty scalers dict still scales every column — there is no pass scalers={} to skip scaling shortcut' (artifact_service.py:881-884). to_model_ready iterates EVERY tag column with method = scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER), and DEFAULT_SCALER = 'minmax' (feature_service.py:79, :546). Client-side dwScalerConfigsAtom starts {} (store/dataset-studio.ts:351); the only control is the opt-in FeatureTransformDialog in Step 4, whose SCALER_OPTIONS offers standard/minmax/robust and NO 'none' (feature-engineering/transformation-panel.tsx:38-59). So zero rules + never opening that dialog => scalers:{} => every column min-max scaled to [0,1]. Exactly reproduces the reported symptom. There is no branch in which the user declined and no affordance to decline.

(2) YES — currentArtifactId IS the scaled frame, on all 5 saved datasets. currentArtifactId -> FINAL -> (promotion by pointer, ADR-DS-LAKE-005B-B-006) -> the GOLD key, i.e. post-to_model_ready. Live DB: all five FINALs resolve to a GOLD-shared/data_gold.parquet key. Surfaces, none of which mention units: dataset-card.tsx:94 (KPIs); dataset-detail-sheet.tsx:122 (KPIs, per-tag statistics, correlation, data preview); the CSV export in that same sheet; pipeline/phase-2-dataset-review.tsx:74 (Model wizard Dataset Review); and dataset-compare-modal.tsx. NEW DEFECT in the last one: the validation sidecar is stored RAW — artifact_service.py:777-784 states validate_frame 'is untouched here: it stays raw/unscaled until prepare_holdout_for_run'. The compare modal therefore drew Box 1 (train = FINAL = scaled [0,1]) against Box 2 (holdout = engineering units) on an IDENTICAL locked Y domain from sharedYDomain(); for a tag spanning ~45,000 the train line collapses to a sliver on the axis floor. The y-lock added as the correctness measure was what made the chart false. Affected both datasets where the modal is reachable (DatasetM1, TestDataset1). Fixed in this task by inverse-transforming the train side (see below) — no pipeline code touched.

(3) INVERTIBLE, with two caveats. build_feature_spec persists scalingParams = exactly what each scaler FIT (feature_spec_service.py:241). Live-confirmed on DatasetM1's GOLD feature_spec.json: ~22 tags each carrying {min,max}. featureSpecKey is NON-NULL on all five adopted FINAL rows, so a consumer starting at currentArtifactId reaches the params directly — no lineage walk. Inverse (minmax): v = scaled*(max-min)+min. CAVEAT A, quantization: _scale_column applies _round_to(x,3) to every scaled value (feature_service.py:450,:463,:483; _round_to at cleaning_service.py:77), so recovered precision is 0.001*span — about +/-45 engineering units on a tag spanning 45,000. Display-adequate, not byte-exact. CAVEAT B, one genuinely non-invertible case: robust with iqr==0 stores 0.0 for every row against {median, iqr:0}. standard/std==0 and minmax/span==0 both invert correctly (all rows equalled the recorded centre). 'none' and robust-with-zero-finite are absent from scalingParams by design — identity, nothing to invert. CONSEQUENCE: display and export can present engineering units from the same bytes; no pipeline change is required for a fix.

(4) NO for the feature frame; BRONZE yes. Live DB, all five saved datasets: 0 live SILVER each; one live GOLD each (the same bytes FINAL points at); BRONZE live for all five. So 'just read the pre-scale artifact' is unavailable. BRONZE is a usable engineering-units fallback but is PRE-FEATURES — raw tags only, no derived columns, and a different row count after cleaning.

(5) THE EXPORT OMITS THE UNIT CHANGE ENTIRELY. Current copy verbatim (dataset-detail-sheet.tsx): '{rowCount} rows, {tags.length} columns. Status columns are not included — a Bad reading exports as a blank cell.' Accurate about status columns; says NOTHING about units. Given read 2 this CSV is a min-max normalized frame presented as the dataset's data. It leaves the system and gets used against historian values — the highest-consequence surface here, and still unaddressed (see follow-ups).

(6) YES, LOAD-BEARING — a fix must not unscale FINAL. images/trainer/train.py is the only trainer. It contains no StandardScaler/MinMaxScaler/RobustScaler/fit_transform anywhere (grep across all of apps/python and images/). It never re-fits and never reads scalingParams; it consumes the pre-scaled bytes directly. It only refuses when target_scaled is true (train.py:416) and gates SVR on feature_spec['scaling'] being non-empty (train.py:269-273). Design intent is explicit and correct: assert_target_is_unscaled (feature_service.py:490) keeps the TARGET in engineering units so predictions come back comparable, while feature inputs are scaled. An unscaled FINAL would therefore be a MODEL-FLOW-breaking change; the fix is disclosure + inverse-on-read, never unscaling the artifact. BONUS DEFECT, same root as read 1: spec['scaling'] is built from sorted(scalers.items()) — the user's EXPLICIT config only (feature_spec_service.py:223-224). Live-confirmed on DatasetM1: 'scaling': [] alongside a populated 'scalingParams' of ~22 min/max entries. So train.py:269 FALSELY REFUSES SVR ('feature_spec.json reports no scaling on the input') on data that IS correctly min-max scaled. A false refusal, not a safety gap — and the two fields disagree about the same artifact.

NO PIPELINE CODE CHANGED, per this task's own instruction. The read-path/UI fix for the read-2 defect (new /v1/preprocess/feature-spec + GET /:id/artifacts/:artifactId/feature-spec, both mirroring the existing column-stats pair, plus inverseScale applied to the compare modal's train series) writes no artifact and alters no stage.

FOLLOW-UPS THIS REPORT SURFACES, each needing its own id: (a) unit disclosure on the CSV export caption and the detail-sheet KPIs (reads 2,5); (b) the scaling-vs-scalingParams disagreement causing the false SVR refusal (read 6); (c) no 'none' scaler option and no disclosed default in Step 4 (read 1).
tasks.scope_note:
REPORTED SYMPTOM: a dataset was fetched with FIC107R.PV in the tens of thousands, taken through Steps 5 and 6 with ZERO cleaning rules applied, and after Save every tag reads below 1. The user's expectation is that a saved dataset holds the values their flow produced.

PREMISE UNDER TEST: that this is unintended scaling. DS-LAKE-024-T00 read 5 predicts otherwise — to_model_ready (feature_service.py:519) runs on the post-split result and returns scaling_params which build_feature_spec persists, so scaling appears to be a designed tail of the features job and FINAL appears to be a MODEL-READY artifact by construction. If that holds, this is not a scaling defect: it is an undisclosed unit change on the one artifact every consumer surface reads. Report which it is; do not assume either.

SIX READS.

(1) WHICH STAGE SCALED IT, AND WAS scale:true CHOSEN OR DEFAULTED? T00 read 6 records that a reordered FEATURE job with scale:false commits SILVER with pipelineVersion 2, so a scale flag exists. Trace every writer of that flag from the client call through the job to to_model_ready. Determine whether the Step 5/6 path the user took sets scale:true explicitly, inherits a default, or has no branch at all. If the user was never offered the choice, that is the finding — separate from whether scaling itself is correct.

(2) WHAT DOES currentArtifactId POINT AT, AND IS THAT THE SCALED FRAME? saveDraftAsDatasetService adopts FINAL and lineage[0] (T00 read 4). Confirm FINAL is the post-to_model_ready frame. If so, every surface reading currentArtifactId — the detail sheet's KPIs, per-tag statistics, correlation, data preview, AND the CSV export — is showing scaled values, and none of them says so. Enumerate the surfaces rather than assuming the sheet is the only one.

(3) IS THE SCALING INVERTIBLE FROM WHAT IS PERSISTED? Read what build_feature_spec writes into scaling_params: per-column method, and the fitted constants (mean/std, or min/max, or whatever to_model_ready produces). Determine whether an exact inverse is reconstructible for every column, including columns whose params are degenerate (std 0, or a constant column). This decides the whole shape of the fix: if invertible, display and export can present engineering units from the same bytes and no pipeline change is needed. If not invertible, the raw values are GONE from FINAL and the only paths are keeping an unscaled artifact or reading further up the lineage.

(4) IS AN UNSCALED FRAME STILL AVAILABLE FOR A SAVED DATASET? The pre-scale frame is the feature artifact. T00 read 4: 0 of 7 SILVER and 0 of 33 GOLD are adopted, 3 SILVER and 28 GOLD already carry objectReclaimedAt, and 2 of 5 saved lineages contain no SILVER link at all. So 'just read the pre-scale artifact' is probably not available. Confirm against the live DB per dataset. The adopted BRONZE IS retained and IS in engineering units — establish whether it is a usable fallback for display, noting it is pre-features so its columns are the raw tags, not the feature columns.

(5) DOES THE EXPORT CLAIM ANYTHING IT NO LONGER MEANS? dataset-detail-sheet.tsx's export caption states only that status columns are excluded and a Bad reading exports blank. It says nothing about units. If read 2 confirms FINAL is scaled, that CSV is a normalized frame presented as the dataset's data — the highest-consequence surface here, because it leaves the system and gets used in reports against historian values. Quote the current copy and state what it omits.

(6) WAS SCALING EVER SUPPOSED TO BE A DATASET CONCERN? Check whether MODEL-FLOW/MODEL-SERVE fits its own scaler at train time or consumes dataset-side scaling_params. If a model refits, the dataset-side scaling is redundant AND destructive. If the model relies on the persisted params, then FINAL being scaled is load-bearing and any change here is a MODEL-FLOW-breaking change. This read decides whether a fix is local or cross-feature.

Write all six answers into this task's result. Do not change any pipeline code in this task — an unscaled FINAL would break every consumer that currently assumes model-ready bytes, and read 6 is what says which those are.

features.title: Compare modal: two-sided Histogram/Box Plot/Correlation (train vs. validation)
features.description: DatasetCompareModal (data-studio/components/dataset-compare-modal.tsx) had only a Line Chart and a Raw Table tab, both already two-sided (train vs. validation holdout). DataAnalysisCard's Histogram/Box Plot/Correlation Heatmap tabs existed only for a single artifact with no validation-side twin. This adds all three to the compare modal in two-sided form, reusing the wizard's presentational chart components (TagHistogramChart/TagBoxplotChart/TagCorrelationChart) rather than mounting DataAnalysisCard itself, which is not reusable here (BoundedSample-typed, reads dw* draft atoms unconditionally, embeds a scaler-config write dialog).
findings: PYTHON NEEDS NO CHANGE. histogram_service.py/boxplot_service.py/correlation_matrix_service.py all load via store.get_frame(request.source_key, ...) — an arbitrary object key, not one bound to an artifact id. The entire backend addition is three new NestJS routes resolving the run's validate_data.parquet sidecar key (via the existing private findHoldoutArtifact + sidecarKey helpers, same lookup /validation-rows and /holdout already use) instead of the artifact's own objectKey.

THE getArtifactValidationRowsService 422-CATCH BRANCH IS DEAD CODE, NOT A PATTERN TO COPY. postToPython never surfaces a 422 to NestJS for this route family: Python maps a missing object to ObjectNotFoundError -> 404, and python-client.ts collapses every other upstream 4xx (including 422) to 400. The three new validation-chart service methods deliberately omit that branch. What a client-facing hook actually sees: 404 = no holdout / sidecar gone, 400 = a requested tag is not a column in the sidecar.

AN UNKNOWN-COLUMN REQUEST FAILS THE WHOLE CHART REQUEST, NOT PER-TAG. A holdout split at BRONZE (pre-features) has raw tags only; Python projects [timestamp, tag, status(tag), ...] before the read, so one derived-feature tag in the request raises inside pyarrow for the ENTIRE call — same discipline getArtifactValidationRowsService's own doc comment already establishes for /validation-rows. The original plan assumed a per-tag partial result could be recovered by intersecting against useArtifactValidationRows' sample.tags; that hook itself all-or-nothing fails the same way, so there is no partial-tag signal to intersect against. Corrected to a tab-level 'tagMismatch' state (set on a 400) with one honest caption, rather than fake per-tag filtering.

POSITIONS VS. SPREADS UNDER INVERSE-SCALING. The train side's histogram/boxplot stats are computed over min-max-scaled-to-[0,1] bytes (DS-LAKE-025-T06) and must be inverted for display. inverseScale's full affine map (scaled*slope+offset) is correct for a POSITION (mean, quantile, KDE x-coordinate) but wrong for a SPREAD (std, range, IQR) — a spread is a difference of two positions and the offset cancels out of a difference, so running it through inverseScale adds the offset back in and produces a plausible-looking wrong number. lib/inverse-scale-stats.ts computes a spread's multiplier as inverseScale(1)-inverseScale(0) (the transform's slope alone) rather than reimplementing per-method arithmetic.

CORRELATION NEEDS NO INVERSION AT ALL. Pearson r is invariant under a positive affine transform, and every scaler this app supports (minmax/standard/robust) has a positive slope — confirmed via the same inverseScale(1)-inverseScale(0) identity. Both sides' correlation matrices are used as the server returned them.

Δr MUST MATCH BY TAG NAME ON THE INTERSECTION, NEVER BY MATRIX INDEX. DraftCorrelationResult.tags is server-resolved (its own doc comment: never assume it equals the request's tags), and the near-constant filter that produces it is not scale-invariant — the scaled train side and the raw validation side can legitimately resolve to different tag sets for a structural reason, not noise. Sending the same <=MAX_TAGS candidate list with an explicit topK (>= the tag cap, so the top-k cut never fires) leaves the near-constant filter as the only remaining divergence source; tags resolved on only one side are named, not silently dropped.

MODEL-FLOW-014-T02 CROSS-LEDGER NOTE (2026-09-01): histogram_service.py, boxplot_service.py and correlation_matrix_service.py -- three of the four services this feature's compare-modal tabs read -- had their sampling changed from frame.head(sample_rows) to services.downsample.systematic_sample (an evenly-spaced sample spanning the WHOLE window, not its earliest contiguous slice). Numbers returned by those three services now differ from what V05's still-pending live check would have seen before this change, for any artifact/window larger than sampleRows -- this feature sends sampleRows=50,000 explicitly, so a real dataset bigger than that moves. The change is a correctness fix (the old head() cut summarised the earliest period, not the requested window), not a regression, but whoever runs V05 should verify against POST-change numbers, not a pre-change expectation. scatter_service.py was also fixed but this feature does not use it.

train_side_reuses_shipped_routes.chosen: Train side reuses the existing POST .../histogram|boxplot|correlation routes unchanged, plus client-side inversion (lib/inverse-scale-stats.ts). Only the validation side gets new backend routes.
train_side_reuses_shipped_routes.rationale: Keeps every inverse-scaling computation in one place and matches DS-LAKE-025-T06's established rule: invert on read for display, never unscale the artifact or a fetched result server-side.

Required adding an optional sampleRows param to the existing wizard-shared hooks (useArtifactHistogram/useArtifactBoxplot/useArtifactCorrelation) and their service methods.

features.title: Edit re-entry survives a reclaimed draft artifact
features.description: Opening Edit on ANY saved dataset showed Step 3's 'Preview sample unavailable — Could not load the preview sample' and never rendered DataAnalysisCard. Verified live against this environment's Postgres + MinIO: every ACTIVE edit draft's currentArtifactId pointed at a GOLD artifact stamped objectReclaimedAt (2026-08-28 / 2026-08-30) whose object was genuinely gone from MinIO, while that same draft's own BRONZE root was unreclaimed AND present. resolveOrCreateEditDraftService's existing-draft early return handed that dead id straight back; the client stored it in dwDraftArtifactIdAtom, which routed the preview fetch onto the draft leg, which 404'd, which the hook's bare catch collapsed into the single sticky state describeAnalysisReadiness maps to phase 'error'.
findings: THE RECLAIM IS CORRECT; THE RE-ENTRY IS NOT. DS-LAKE-014 deliberately makes an ACTIVE draft's own artifacts reclaim-eligible after activeIdleHours of inactivity (artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts's ACTIVE branch, a recorded reversal of DS-LAKE-009B's unconditional skip), and cleanup stamped every row properly. The defect is that resolveOrCreateEditDraftService's 200 branch returned currentArtifactId without ever checking objectReclaimedAt — while the 201 branch immediately below it already refuses a reclaimed dataset root with a tailored 422. The check existed; it was simply on one path and not the other.

THE DRAFT'S OWN BRONZE ROOT IS A RELIABLE RECOVERY TARGET, VERIFIED. For all four affected drafts the GOLD's parentArtifactId chain terminates at a BRONZE owned by the SAME draft, and every one of those roots is unreclaimed with its object present. That is not luck: the edit draft's root is a share-by-pointer row over the saved dataset's own BRONZE (DS-LAKE-024), so protectedObjectKeys (DS-LAKE-024-T05) pins it against exactly this sweep.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT BUG IN THE SAME METHOD. The 201 create branch sets currentArtifactId in a tx.datasetDraft.update whose result is discarded, then serializes the captured pre-update draft — so a dataset's FIRST edit received currentArtifactId: null and dwDraftArtifactIdAtom stayed null for the whole session, leaving useDatasetGoldWarm / useDatasetHoldoutResplit / useDatasetDraftPipeline running id-less. It stayed invisible because a null id is exactly what routes the preview card onto the dataset leg, which reads the still-live adopted BRONZE. The existing create-branch spec asserted the draft/artifact args and rootValidationRowCount but never currentArtifactId.

THE USER'S 'PATH FILE CHANGE' HYPOTHESIS IS RULED OUT. Object keys legitimately vary across datasets in this environment (drafts/{id}/.../data.parquet, drafts/{id}/.../data_bronze.parquet, {datasetId}/.../data_bronze.parquet) and all resolve: DS-LAKE-016's stage suffixes only ever WIDENED the accepted filename set (artifact-keys.ts's ALL_DATA_FILENAMES keeps the legacy data.parquet), backend and Python filename maps are string-for-string identical, and Save repoints the row's objectKey at adoption time. What broke is a reclaimed id being handed back, not a renamed path.

THE CLIENT COLLAPSES EVERY FAILURE INTO ONE STICKY STATE. use-dataset-feature-preview-sample.ts's bare `catch {}` discards the status, and dataset-readiness.ts maps previewFetchState === 'error' to a phase that hides the card entirely, so a policy-driven cleanup and a genuine transport failure were indistinguishable to the user. The hook also sent NO tags, against the explicit warning in datasetArtifactService.rows' own doc comment (DS-LAKE-012 found that omission live).

self_heal_rather_than_refuse.chosen: On resolve, if currentArtifactId is reclaimed, walk to the draft's own live BRONZE root via the existing resolvePristineBronzeRoot and re-point currentArtifactId at it, persisted. Refuse with the create branch's own 422 only when that root is reclaimed too.
self_heal_rather_than_refuse.rationale: The root is still readable and still pinned, so refusing would strand the user on a dataset that is perfectly editable. Re-pointing costs only the feature warm Step 4 recomputes anyway, and persisting it means the Step 5 clean/scale commit and the holdout re-split — which read the same column — are fixed by the same write. Abandon-and-recreate was considered and rejected: it discards the draft's other state and writes more rows to reach the same artifact.

check_the_ledger_not_the_bytes.chosen: recoverReclaimedEditDraftRoot reads objectReclaimedAt, not object storage.
check_the_ledger_not_the_bytes.rationale: Cleanup stamps and never deletes rows (stampReclaimed), so the stamp is the authoritative signal and costs one indexed read instead of a Python round trip on every resolve. The unstamped-but-missing case (bytes deleted outside the ledger, recorded in DS-LAKE-025's findings) is deliberately NOT covered here — listDraftRowsService's own guard reports it honestly rather than this method inventing a recovery for a state it cannot verify.

tasks.result: dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts: new private recoverReclaimedEditDraftRoot(draft) — probes the current artifact's objectReclaimedAt, and on a stamped row resolves the draft's BRONZE root through the existing resolvePristineBronzeRoot (a pure row walk, so a reclaimed starting point is fine), persists currentArtifactId, and reports recovered: true. Applied to BOTH 200 paths: the existing-ACTIVE-draft early return and the P2002 race-winner fallback, which can be just as stale. Refuses with the create branch's own 422 when the root is reclaimed too. mapDraft's callers now also emit recoveredFromReclaimedArtifact.

tasks.title: Return the shared root id from the create branch
tasks.result: The 201 response now spreads `...this.mapDraft({ ...draft, currentArtifactId: sharedRoot.id })` instead of serializing the pre-update row. One line, but it is what makes a dataset's first edit populate dwDraftArtifactIdAtom at all.

tasks.title: Typed error when a draft-scoped read hits reclaimed bytes
tasks.result: New private resolveReadableDraftArtifactKey(draftId, artifactId) returns the objectKey or throws — 404 for a row that does not resolve, 422 naming the reclaim for a stamped one — instead of letting a dead key reach Python and surface as an opaque 404. Wired into the five draft-scoped reads that actually fetch bytes: listDraftRowsService plus the histogram / boxplot / scatter / correlation services. Deliberately NOT applied to the metadata, tag-catalog or job-start lookups, which read the row or a sidecar and outlive the reclaim by design.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CODEBASE.md do not describe apps/python, MinIO, object storage, the dataset models or background jobs at all. Updating them is worthwhile but is documentation work, not part of this refactor.
Apache Iceberg or another table-format migration. The v3 path remains MinIO + Parquet; adopt Iceberg only if measured dataset/version scale requires table-format metadata and snapshot management.
One-file-per-tag Parquet partitioning. The layout must be benchmarked first; small-file explosion is explicitly out of scope until measurements justify a partition strategy.
Multi-replica distributed job ownership remains deferred as already documented.
global_definition_of_done: MinIO is the single source of truth; Postgres stores metadata and pointers only.
Every processing stage produces its own immutable artifact.
No artifact is ever overwritten; a new run produces a new artifact.
Every artifact records its parent, so lineage supports audit and reproduction.
Every artifact carries a checksum computed at write time.
Validation is mandatory and a FAIL blocks the commit.
A Dataset Version is created only by Save Dataset.
Intermediate stages never create a Dataset Version.
Dataset rows are never stored in the Dataset Registry.
Promotion changes metadata only; no artifact is copied or regenerated.
Saving a Dataset never creates a Model and never starts training.
The browser never owns the full Dataset for large artifacts; metadata, viewport rows and bounded previews are separate concerns.
Server-side pagination/filtering and frontend virtualization are both used for large dataset browsing.
Cleaning and feature engineering operate on server-side artifacts; selecting all tags never requires a full browser payload.
Intermediate artifacts are retained by policy and cleaned only after the final persistence boundary is safe.
Cleanup is independent of Save success and cannot delete referenced FINAL/registry artifacts.
The five-step wizard UX is unchanged.
No use of any and no @ts-ignore.
Errors are raised as AppException from @softsensor/common, never as raw Nest HTTP exceptions.
Multi-step writes that must succeed together run in a Prisma transaction.
Every feature is marked completed only after its acceptance criteria and verification items are actually verified, not merely implemented.
Numeric row and preview payloads cross the wire as columnar binary (Arrow IPC), never as JSON arrays of numbers.
No endpoint returns more than max_points per series without server-side downsampling, and a before/after pair always shares one bucket basis so a visible diff is never the sampler's.
Cleanup reclaims MinIO objects only; DatasetArtifact rows are never deleted because they are the audit trail and they carry the recipe.
An artifact reachable through the parentArtifactId chain of a non-ARCHIVED DatasetVersion is pinned, and retention age cannot release it.
Every bounded rule is unconditional -- there is no 'large dataset' threshold and therefore no second unbounded code path.
Client transform libraries accept a bounded sample type; passing a full frame is a compile error, not a code-review question.
The Loader sink interface assumes a narrow serving schema; no design step may assume an 8,000-tag frame can be loaded wide.

draft_architecture.entity: DatasetDraft { id, name?, workspaceId, sourceIds[], status ACTIVE|SAVED|ABANDONED, currentArtifactId?, savedDatasetId?, createdById, createdAt, updatedAt } with artifacts[] and jobs[] back-relations.
draft_architecture.ownership_rule: DatasetArtifact and PreprocessingJob each carry BOTH datasetId? and draftId?, with a CHECK constraint per table: (datasetId IS NOT NULL OR draftId IS NOT NULL).
draft_architecture.why_nullable: READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING IT. The instruction "do not make PreprocessingJob.datasetId nullable" and the rule "must reference either a Draft or a Dataset, never neither" can only both hold if the COLUMN is nullable and a CHECK does the enforcing — a NOT NULL datasetId cannot coexist with a draft-owned job. The column is nullable; it is never unconstrained.
draft_architecture.both_set_is_legal: Adoption at Save sets datasetId while KEEPING draftId, so a saved artifact stays traceable to the run that produced it. The CHECK permits both deliberately.
draft_architecture.minio_layout: drafts/{draftId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/data.parquet, with the DS-LAKE-003 sidecars beside it. The earlier drafts/{userId}/... proposal is DROPPED: the DatasetDraft row carries createdById, so ownership is a database fact and does not need to be smuggled into the object key.
draft_architecture.source_scoping: CRITICAL, carried over unchanged in intent. Draft materialize must scope the DataSource lookup to DatasetDraft.sourceIds, exactly as the dataset path scopes to Dataset.sourceIds (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts:224). The secret is decrypted server-side, so an unconstrained lookup would let a caller name an arbitrary source id and have the server connect with that source credentials.
draft_architecture.adoption_not_copying: Save sets datasetId on the existing artifact rows and leaves objectKey untouched. No artifact is copied, rewritten or regenerated — required by the slice global_definition_of_done.

frontend: Preview is selected-tag/time-window bounded and server-downsampled
Numeric payloads arrive as Arrow IPC and decode into the columnar TypedArray store
Large tables are virtualized on both axes
No full Dataset clone/materialisation, at any dataset size
Client transform libraries are reachable only with a bounded sample type
backend: NestJS orchestrates DatasetDraft, jobs, persistence boundary and access contracts
No timeseries rows in registry tables
python: FastAPI owns dataset processing and query boundary
Parquet-native query path is benchmarked and used for large artifacts
Series responses are LTTB-downsampled with a declared ratio and a shared bucket basis
storage: Sidecar manifest/checksum/feature spec/validation report/column stats remain metadata artifacts
Intermediate artifacts use explicit retention and cleanup, with transitive-lineage pinning
serving: Loader is asynchronous and independent of Save
The sink interface assumes a narrow schema; a wide 8,000-tag load is not representable in PostgreSQL
TimescaleDB remains deferred until infrastructure is explicitly introduced
